key_contributions: Adapts shared spatiotemporal features to heterogeneous monocular UAV scenes with anchor-conditioned feature aggregation.
Separates anchor-state motion from local Gaussian geometry through decoupled local deformation.
Warps feature-query coordinates according to non-uniform anchor density and evaluates on UAV-Arc4D, VisDrone, and UAVDT.
papers.title: AdaAnchor4D: Anchor-Conditioned Spatiotemporal Feature Aggregation for Monocular UAV 4D Reconstruction

key_contributions: Defines a temporal extension of SOG for model-agnostic, index-aligned 4D Gaussian storage.
Adds per-Gaussian timelines and image-backed temporal parameterizations for geometry and appearance attributes.
Evaluates storage and rendered quality against PLY-sequence and FreeTimeGS baselines, and demonstrates PlayCanvas playback.
papers.title: TSOG: A Format For Temporally And Spatially Ordered Gaussians

key_contributions: Generates text-conditioned dynamic humans directly in 4D Gaussian space instead of fitting a representation to generated videos.
Combines a 3D U-Net with temporal attention, 2D regularization, and training-free 4D interpolation for view and motion consistency.
Constructs 60,000 text-to-4DGS training pairs and produces 360-degree dynamic humans within one minute.
papers.title: 4DHumanDiff: Direct Text-to-4DGS Generation for Consistent 360-Degree Dynamic Humans

key_contributions: Reconstructs articulated objects with explicit part structure rather than relying on photometric supervision alone.
Uses oriented part bounding boxes to constrain spatial coherence and preserve contact between adjacent movable parts.
Adds structure-aware losses that sharpen part boundaries and reduce geometric artifacts during Gaussian optimization.
papers.title: StructureGS: Structure-aware Gaussian Splatting for Articulated Object Reconstruction

key_contributions: Decomposes dynamic Gaussian scenes into quality and resolution layers with inter-layer predictive coding.
Adds temporal B-frames and a lightweight transformer for cross-layer and temporal prediction.
Packetizes Gaussians by volume-opacity importance and maps the scalable bitstream to MPEG-DASH sub-representations.
papers.title: SplatStream: Fine Granular Scalable Gaussian Splatting for Adaptive 3D Scene Streaming

key_contributions: Builds a hybrid head avatar with explicit Gaussian hair strands and unstructured Gaussians for the face and upper body.
Models hair inertia with an LSTM conditioned on head angular velocity, acceleration, and relative gravity, followed by FiLM-modulated strand deformation.
Jointly optimizes appearance and motion using photometric, geometric, and physics-based supervision from synchronized multi-view video.
papers.title: Head Avatars with Dynamic Explicit Hair

key_contributions: Represents video with static 3D Gaussians whose opacity follows a learnable continuous temporal mean and scale.
Lets Gaussian components fade in and out without a spatial deformation field, preserving compatibility with standard 3D editing tools.
Uses off-the-shelf pose estimates to stabilize the static spatial geometry for manual and physics-based edits.
papers.title: TOM-GS: Editable Video Representation via Temporal Opacity Modulation of Static 3D Gaussians

key_contributions: To address these issues, the paper presents GrainGS, a dynamic Gaussian framework that combines a hierarchical anchor scaffold with per-Gaussian deformation.
Experiments on synthetic monocular and real-world multiview benchmarks show that GrainGS achieves high reconstruction quality, real-time novel view synthesis, and compact storage.
A static warm-up stage first establishes a time-invariant canonical representation from observations across all timestamps.
papers.title: GrainGS: Gradient-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

key_contributions: Proposes FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation, while simultaneously enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery.
The core of the method lies in a thorough analysis of the attention mechanisms and the entangled reconstruction and animation training pipeline adopted by prior state-of-the-art approaches.

The analysis identifies two main factors that compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between the tasks of reconstruction and animation.
papers.title: FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head

key_contributions: To overcome this limitation, the paper introduces FlexiAvatar, a unified framework that explicitly optimizes only the visible body regions, effectively eliminating artifacts arising from unobserved limbs.
The method integrates occlusion-robust SMPL-X tracking with part-specific residual refinement to capture high-frequency geometric and appearance details.

Experiments on full-body (NeuMan, ZJU-MoCap, WildAvatar), talk-show half-body, and INSTA head inputs report consistently higher reconstruction quality, with roughly 3% average PSNR improvement over prior methods.
papers.title: FlexiAvatar: Unified 3D Gaussian Human Avatars Under Arbitrary Body Visibility

key_contributions: Presents AniGS, a method for scene-level animation of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstructions that adds subtle, distributed dynamics, e.g., vegetation motion, while preserving rigid structures.

To animate the entire scene, the method leverages a pretrained video diffusion model and introduce an iterative dataset--model update strategy that progressively expands viewpoint coverage and repeatedly updates camera-fixed training videos using a render-and-refine scheme.

Experiments on five real-world, large-scale outdoor scenes demonstrate that AniGS produces natural ambient dynamics and high-quality novel view videos, enabling more immersive viewing experiences of reconstructed environments.
papers.title: AniGS: Bridging Rendering and Diffusion Prior for 3D Scene Animation

key_contributions: Introduces SPIN-4DGS, which learns Gaussian attributes from explicitly collected spatiotemporal positions instead of modeling temporal displacements.
Uses a lightweight feed-forward network under rasterization-based reconstruction loss to avoid optimizing attributes explicitly at every spatiotemporal position.
Shares representations across Gaussians to improve spatiotemporal consistency under large inter-frame motion.
papers.title: Implicit 4D Gaussian Splatting for Fast Motion with Large Inter-Frame Displacements

key_contributions: Introduces Grassmannian splatting, whose Gaussian primitives lie on rank-three planes in spacetime and condition to rank-two surfels at each frame.
Encodes primitive orientation, normal velocity, disk shape, and tangential drift in a closed-form motion model without a learned deformation field.
Uses a standard 3DGS rasterizer and reports substantially faster training while remaining competitive on MonoDyGauBench.
papers.title: Grassmannian Splatting I: Moving rank-2 Spacetime Surfels for Dynamic Scene Rendering

key_contributions: Reconstructs dynamic human scenes from sparse, low-overlap cameras by separating the background and people into complementary Gaussian representations.
Densifies background supervision by synthesizing hundreds of camera-controlled novel views with a video diffusion model.
Initializes deformable humans through cross-view identity association and triangulated keypoints, then harmonizes the composed scene with motion-adaptive diffusion refinement.
papers.title: 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction from Low-Overlap Captures

key_contributions: To address these limitations, the paper proposes Track2Map, an online 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline that jointly optimizes camera trajectory and 3D deformable scene representation directly from surgical video.
To stabilize optimization in the presence of tissue motion and ambiguous visual cues, the paper introduces a track-anchored deformation initialization using dense 2D point tracks.
Experiments on StereoMIS show improved reconstruction quality and camera trajectory against competing SLAM methods, as well as compared to non-SLAM methods that utilize camera trajectory priors.
papers.title: Track2Map: Online Deformable SLAM with Motion-Aware Pose Optimization in Robotic Surgery

key_contributions: Systematically studies mixture-of-experts designs for dynamic Gaussian deformation instead of treating the expert architecture as an implementation detail.
Introduces MoDE, which jointly trains shared canonical experts to specialize in complementary motion patterns.
Presents MoE-GS as a second design with independently trained experts and a learned router for combining their predictions.
papers.title: On the Design of Mixture-of-Experts for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To unify these aspects within a single framework, the paper proposes CARLA-GS, a modular corner-case synthesis pipeline that decouples visual representation, semantic reasoning, and physics-based execution while maintaining tight cross-module coupling.

Experiments on the Waymo Open Dataset show, both quantitatively and qualitatively, that the framework enables controllable corner-case generation and produces photorealistic, spatiotemporally consistent videos aligned with semantic intent and physically feasible motion.
Starting from real driving data, the method reconstructs an editable gaussian scene with additional geometry-consistent constraints.
papers.title: CARLA-GS: Decoupling Representation, Reasoning, and Physics Simulation for Autonomous Driving Corner-Case Synthesis

key_contributions: To fill this gap, the paper presents GUSH3R (Gaussian-Unified Scene Human 3D Reconstruction), a feed-forward framework for online dynamic human-scene reconstruction.
Reconstructs dynamic humans and static scenes as geometrically consistent 3DGS primitives in one feed-forward pass from monocular video.

Experiments on monocular human-scene datasets demonstrate that the approach achieves competitive novel view synthesis quality while significantly improving inference efficiency compared to optimization-based methods.
papers.title: GUSH3R: Everyone Everywhere All at Once as Gaussians

key_contributions: Uses shared HexPlane kinematic latents to synchronize semantic evolution with scene dynamics while decoupling semantics from geometric deformation.
Introduces rasterization-native semantic extraction from topologically continuous feature maps to reduce sensitivity to reconstruction artifacts.
Optimizes semantic features in their hyperspherical latent space to preserve semantic-anatomic alignment under tissue deformation and topology changes.
papers.title: DeGenseGS: Geometrically and Semantically Decoupled Surgical Scene Understanding in 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Proposes PhysMani, a framework that couples a physics-principled 3D Gaussian world model with a future-aware action policy model.
The policy model integrates the predicted 3D scene future dynamics through a learnable token based cross-attention module.
The world model learns a divergence-free Gaussian velocity field via online optimization for fast and physically grounded future dynamics prediction.
papers.title: PhysMani: Physics-principled 3D World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation

key_contributions: To overcome these limitations, the paper presents DL-SLAM, a monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM system built upon a novel dual-level probabilistic framework.
The method computes dynamic probability maps by combining semantic and geometric information.
Experimental results demonstrate that DL-SLAM outperforms existing approaches, improving tracking accuracy by up to 13% while generating high-fidelity semantic maps.
papers.title: DL-SLAM: Enabling High-Fidelity Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environments based on Dual-Level Probability

key_contributions: Reformulates monocular 4D synthesis as scene completion that must infer regions beyond observed-view interpolation.
Unifies training and inference through panoramic trajectory guidance to improve cross-view consistency under large viewpoint deviations.
Distills panoramic generative content into explicit dynamic Gaussians to preserve motion scale, shape, and other physical scene priors.
papers.title: Unified Panoramic-Gaussian Representation for Monocular 4D Scene Synthesis

key_contributions: Aggregates per-Gaussian deformation statistics over time to estimate motion variance and guide dynamic-static separation.
Introduces MotionFormer, which applies temporal self-attention over neighboring timestamps to model local motion dependencies.
Improves foreground deformation, temporal consistency, and static-background recovery on dynamic and distractor-free reconstruction benchmarks.
papers.title: MVFusion-GS: Motion-Variance Guided Temporal Attention for High-Quality Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Presents World from Motion, a method for generating freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian representations from monocular videos.
To train this model, the method constructs a dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3DGS representations, with simulated artifacts characteristic of monocular reconstruction.

The approach conditions a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion along both input and target camera trajectories to correct rendering artifacts and fill in missing regions.
papers.title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video

key_contributions: Presents GaussianEmoTalker, an audio-driven framework for real-time emotional talking head synthesis based on 3D Gaussian Splatting.
To fuse these heterogeneous signals, the paper introduces a spatial-audio-emotion attention module that estimates the offsets of Gaussian attributes for expressive and temporally stable rendering.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that GaussianEmoTalker achieves competitive video quality, accurate lip synchronization, controllable emotional expression, and real-time rendering compared with recent emotional talking head methods.
papers.title: GaussianEmoTalker: Real-Time Emotional Talking Head Synthesis with Audio-Driven and Blendshape-Based 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Proposes LUNA, an LBS-free universal neural animation model that directly maps multiple 2D controls like images, keypoints, sketches, and unseen characters into 3D Gaussian deformations, bypassing explicit body fitting.

To resolve the inherent ambiguity of 2D-to-3D lifting while scaling beyond fitted datasets, the paper introduces hybrid supervision that distills soft structural priors from an LBS teacher and a loss that supports training on both.

Extensive experiments show LUNA achieves competitive visual fidelity compared to LBS-based approaches, while delivering realistic human motion and zero-shot cross-identity generalization across diverse driving modalities.
papers.title: LUNA: Learning Universal 3D Human Animation Beyond Skinning

key_contributions: Presents FFAvatar, a Transformer-based 3D Gaussian framework for fast construction of high-quality and animatable 4D head avatars from one or more reference portrait images.

At the core of the method is an alternating attention mechanism that disentangles identity appearance from expression and viewpoint variations, enabling the reconstruction of a canonical 3D appearance that remains consistent across poses and facial.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that FFAvatar efficiently produces high-fidelity and controllable 4D head avatars, achieving superior flexibility, driving efficiency, and identity-consistent rendering across diverse expressions and viewpoints.
papers.title: FFAvatar: Feed-Forward 4D Head Avatar Reconstruction from Sparse Portrait Images

key_contributions: Extends 4D volumes with time-varying Gaussian means and covariances and derives a velocity field from the representation.
Extends splatting to render camera-motion-aware optical flow, providing dense supervision for dynamics from monocular video.
Improves reconstruction quality while reducing training time and increasing rendering speed.
papers.title: Learning Efficient 4D Gaussian Representations from Monocular Videos with Flow Splatting

key_contributions: Presents HiReFF, a feed-forward method for 2K-resolution 360° human video reconstruction from uncalibrated sparse-view videos.

The framework decomposes the problem into two key tasks: foreground 3D Gaussian reconstruction from sparse-view videos (four views separated by 90°) and computationally efficient high-resolution synthesis.
Experiments demonstrate that HiReFF significantly outperforms existing methods in high-resolution streaming volumetric video reconstruction.
papers.title: HiReFF: High-Resolution Feedforward Human Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Sparse-View Video

key_contributions: Introduces RAGA, a Ray-Traced Gaussian Shadow Casting formulation based on exact ray-Gaussian line integrals.
In contrast to prior methods that rely on binary hit tests and mesh-based shadow casters, the method performs shadow computation entirely in Gaussian space, without requiring any mesh reconstruction.

For each occluding Gaussian, the method integrates the opacity profile along the shadow ray and normalize by the theoretical maximum integral, producing a weight that captures how the ray traverses the occluder rather than merely.
papers.title: RAGA: Real Time Ray Traced Gaussian Shadow Casting for 3DGS Avatar-Scene Interaction

key_contributions: Proposes DLGStream, a novel language-embedded FVV representation that streams time-varying language features alongside Gaussian attributes to support 4D environment interaction, scene editing, and spatial intelligence.

Specifically, the paper proposes a dual-opacity dynamic language Gaussian representation, which maintains two opacity attributes for color and language features to deal with performance degradation that occurs when colors and features are jointly optimized.
Experimental results demonstrate that DLGStream achieves superior performance in both on open-vocabulary segmentation and reconstruction quality with an average frame size of merely 43 KB.
papers.title: DLGStream: Dynamic Language-embedded Guassian Splatting for Open-vocabulary Enabled Free-viewpoint Video Streaming

key_contributions: Presents CoGS, a compositional Gaussian-splatting framework for monocular human--object scene reconstruction.

Experiments on HOSNeRF and NeuMan show that CoGS improves both human--object interaction reconstruction and in-the-wild human--scene rendering, achieving stronger fidelity and perceptual quality across full-frame and human-focused evaluations.
Decomposes each video into articulated-human, rigid-object, and static-scene Gaussian branches.
papers.title: CoGS: Compositional Dynamic Human-Object Scenes Gaussian Splatting from Monocular Video

key_contributions: To address this limitation, the paper introduces a semantics-guided framework that enforces dynamic regularization at the object level, aiming to achieve spatially consistent object-wise deformation.
Specifically, the method firsts extract segmentation masks using the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and derive semantic features from input images.

Experimental results demonstrate that the semantics-aware regularization improves object-level deformation consistency and outperforms baseline methods in rendering quality, achieving higher PSNR and SSIM and lower LPIPS in dynamic 3DGS rendering.
papers.title: SemDynReg: Semantics-Guided Deformation Regularization for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces FiCA, a Feed-forward, instant Gaussian Codec Avatar generation pipeline that creates lifelike avatars from a single portrait image.

Additionally, the paper introduces a feed-forward mesh refinement network that enhances the fidelity and identity preservation of the generated avatars, eliminating the need for person-specific test-time optimization.

Generating a photorealistic and drivable avatar from just a single image is significantly challenging due to the limited visual information available to accurately infer the 3D appearance and geometry of human heads.
papers.title: FiCA: Feed-forward instant Gaussian Codec Avatars from a Single Portrait Image

key_contributions: Proposes MeGAS, a novel framework that incorporates thermomechanical phase-change dynamics into 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS).

Specifically, the paper proposes a new thermomechanical dynamic Gaussian Splatting representation that augments 3DGS with temperature attributes and employs a heat advection-diffusion solver with MPM dynamics incorporating phase transitions, enabling physically plausible and visually realistic.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeGAS produces physically consistent thermomechanical behavior while maintaining high-fidelity photorealistic rendering, advancing toward physics-integrated world models.
papers.title: MeGAS: Thermomechanical Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Thermophysical Scene Editing

key_contributions: Introduces visibility-aware densification so Gaussians are refined according to their actual temporal presence.
Adjusts each Gaussian's densification threshold according to its temporal lifespan through temporally adaptive thresholding.
Uses temporal offset warping to increase deformation capacity near temporal centers and improve reconstruction of highly dynamic regions.
papers.title: Temporally Aware Densification for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Represents a dynamic scene with static, persistent, and transient Gaussian subsets tailored to different temporal behaviors.
Uses competitive residual allocation and shared rasterization to assign scene content across the three representation levels.
Exposes persistent Gaussians as stable primitives for efficient segmentation and tracking in addition to novel-view synthesis.
papers.title: Multi4D: High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Multi-Level Competitive Allocation

key_contributions: Introduces a feed-forward framework for reconstructing dynamic 4D hands directly from egocentric video.
Uses a mesh-guided representation and temporal convolutions to provide structural priors and model hand motion.
Uses Gaussian-splatting image supervision without requiring 3D hand-pose ground truth.
papers.title: Hand-4DGS: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for 4D Hand Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos

key_contributions: Introduces a training-free and mask-free method for recovering object-level structure directly from 4D Gaussian primitives.
Builds a sparse affinity graph from appearance, orientation, scale, deformation trajectories, and rendered-boundary cues.
Partitions the graph with Leiden community detection, avoiding foundation models and learned feature fields while improving segmentation efficiency.
papers.title: Intrinsic 4D Gaussian Segmentation from Scene Cues

key_contributions: Presents Edit3DGS, a unified framework for dynamic 3D head editing that integrates 2D instruction-guided diffusion with 3D Gaussian splatting.

Unlike prior approaches that separately address frame-based edits or static 3D reconstruction, the method couples semantic controllability in the image domain with photorealistic, temporally consistent 3D representations.

Experimental results demonstrate that the framework enables controllable, artifact-free head editing with smooth temporal transitions, offering practical applications in virtual avatars, immersive communication, film production, and interactive media.
papers.title: Edit3DGS: Unified Framework for Dynamic Head Editing via 2D Instruction-Guided Diffusion and 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Combines a feed-forward generator, K-source mean pooling, and monocular-to-multiview training on FLAME-bound Gaussians.
Introduces a 10K-iter layout-preserving per-subject refinement loop that freezes the FLAME-binding and Gaussian count and replaces densification with a three-component anti-spike regularization.

On VFHQ/HDTF cross-domain zero-shot the method surpasses the in-domain leader GAGAvatar by +1.5 dB PSNR despite never training on either test domain, and on the SplattingAvatar monocular benchmark the method leads every reported metric, surpassing.
papers.title: SpatialAvatar-0: High-Quality 4D Head Avatar with Multi-Stage Reconstruction

key_contributions: Generates synchronized dense multi-view videos from monocular or sparse-view dynamic-subject footage using relative camera-pose conditioning.
Uses a five-axis positional encoding and staged curriculum for pose following, view generation, and temporal rollout before downstream 4DGS reconstruction.
Adds multi-view captions for test-time text control and supports mixed human-animal training.
papers.title: Flex4DHuman: Flexible Multi-view Video Diffusion for 4D Human Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces a self-supervised feed-forward framework for pose-free future-view extrapolation in driving scenes.
Predicts future camera parameters through iterative denoising and models nonlinear dynamics with temporal attention and conditioned motion lifting.
Uses progressive training to stabilize unsupervised motion learning against error accumulation.
papers.title: Envision4D: Envisioning Visual Futures via Feed-forward 4D Gaussian Splatting for Autonomous Driving

key_contributions: Presents LentiAvatar, a Gaussian head-avatar system that connects monocular avatar capture with subpixel-encoded glasses-free lenticular display for real-time autostereoscopic communication.
From a monocular portrait video, LentiAvatar reconstructs a controllable head avatar and optimizes it for the lateral viewing zones induced by the display.

The method uses natural head turns as pseudo-multiview (PMV) supervision to constrain regions that are otherwise weakly observed in monocular training, including hair, ears, jaw contours, and neck boundaries.
papers.title: LentiAvatar: Pseudo-Multiview Reconstruction and Subpixel Prism Rendering for Real-Time Stereoscopic Communication

key_contributions: Introduces Self-Adaptive Gaussian Expression (SAGE), a framework for self-learning expression-induced Gaussian deformations that enables high-fidelity, animatable avatars from minimal input data.
Jointly optimizes 2D Gaussian surfels and an SDF, then self-supervises expression deformation with geometric and appearance consistency.
Experiments demonstrate that the approach achieves reconstruction and animation quality comparable to state-of-the-art methods, while reducing data requirements by several orders of magnitude.
papers.title: Self-Learning Expression Deformations for Data-Efficient Gaussian Avatars

key_contributions: Introduces AvatarMix, a compositional paradigm that bypasses these issues by directly composing the head and body from two high-fidelity Gaussian avatars.

To this end, the paper proposes a two-tier refinement strategy: SeamFix, a localized diffusion module that refines hair and neck to ensure an artifact-free join, and an optional full-body refinement, FullbodyFix, that restores garment appearance.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method achieves state-of-the-art results in outfit fidelity and identity preservation, providing a new perspective for realistic 3D outfit personalization.
papers.title: AvatarMix: Identity-Preserving Cross-Avatar Composition for Outfit Personalization

key_contributions: Couples per-object Gaussians and collision meshes to differentiable rigid-body simulation for fully occluded motion.
Estimates friction and velocity before occlusion and uses the simulated SE(3) trajectory to preserve object permanence.
Introduces a centroid-silhouette loss that isolates positional gradients from appearance noise.
papers.title: PersistGS: Differentiable Physics for Object Permanence in 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces timestamp-conditioned learnable Gaussian query tokens that aggregate full temporal context for feed-forward 4D reconstruction.
Decodes Gaussians whose positions are modulated by target time, enabling globally coherent motion modeling without per-scene optimization.
Extends feature aggregation to a 4D feature field for point tracking and dynamic scene understanding, with video-diffusion rendering enhancement.
papers.title: Learning Global Motion with Compact Gaussians for Feed-Forward 4D Reconstruction

key_contributions: To mitigate these limitations, the paper proposes a novel dynamic reconstruction framework built upon an efficient static-dynamic decomposition strategy using a Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting encoder and an optical flow model.

By eliminating redundant computations on static regions, the method achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing baselines across rendering quality, training and rendering speed, and storage efficiency.
Notably, on the Neural 3D dataset, the framework requires only 10 minutes for training and achieves a rendering speed of over 700 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU at resolution of 1352x1014.
papers.title: DSD-GS: Dynamic-Static Decomposition of Gaussian Splatting for Efficient and High-Fidelity Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces R5DGS, which augments a rigid-body-constrained 4D Gaussian representation with compact identity codes for object association.
Uses semantic grouping and rigid motion constraints to reduce deformation ambiguity and improve dynamic-scene efficiency.
Targets accurate reconstruction with fewer redundant Gaussians and more interpretable object-level motion.
papers.title: R5DGS: Semantic-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting with Rigid Body Constraints for Efficient Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Represents a scene with static, rigid, and transient Gaussian primitives for background, long-term motion, and short-term dynamics.
Uses an object-wise dynamic mask to aggregate long-range motion information and separate static from dynamic regions.
Optimizes rigid and transient primitives with scene-flow guidance to provide dense 3D motion supervision.
papers.title: RiGS: Rigid-aware 4D Gaussian Splatting from a Single Monocular Video

key_contributions: To address this, the paper proposes 4D-GSW, a kinematic-aware watermarking framework designed to embed robust copyright information while preserving high spatio-temporal consistency.
Introduces a Spatio-Temporal Curvature (STC) metric to identify "Dynamic Instants," adaptively gating watermark gradient injection to shield critical motion manifolds from non-physical perturbations.

Extensive experiments have demonstrated the superior performance of the method in robustly hiding watermarks while resisting various attacks and maintaining high rendering quality and spatiotemporal consistency.
papers.title: 4D-GSW: Kinematic-Aware Spatio-Temporal Consistent Watermarking for 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces a feed-forward system for dynamic multi-view reconstruction with unknown camera poses.
Decomposes Gaussian motion into image-plane shifts and depth changes, enabling pseudo optical-flow supervision for its 2D component.
Adds bidirectional motion encoding and view-dependent opacity to aggregate features and mitigate Gaussian misalignment.
papers.title: No Pose, No Problem in 4D: Feed-Forward Dynamic Gaussians from Unposed Multi-View Videos

key_contributions: Proposes Decoder-Side Gaussian Splatting (DSGS), a framework that natively replaces the depth-estimation stage of DSDE with feed-forward 3DGS inference, optimizing volumetric scenes entirely on the decoder side from compressed textures and metadata.

A central, counterintuitive finding is that lossy compression acts as an implicit low-pass filter stabilizing feed-forward splat prediction: compressed bitstreams exceed lossless quality while shrinking tenfold.
With four input views, improves BD-PSNR by 5.79 dB and BD-SSIM by 0.054 while reducing maximum inter-view Delta IV-PSNR from 17.2 dB.
papers.title: A Single Atlas is All You Need: Decoder-Side Gaussian Splatting for Immersive Video

key_contributions: Proposes a unified framework that achieves physics-aware reconstruction and physical simulation of endoscopic scenes through Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs)-guided Gaussian Splatting.

To achieve automatic inference of physical properties, the paper introduces an object-wise material field that initializes material parameters via MLLM and refines them through a differentiable Material Point Method (MPM) under joint supervision from rendered.
The approach utilizes 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) integrated with pre-trained segmentation and depth estimation to represent deformable tissues and tools.
papers.title: EndoGSim: Physics-Aware 4D Dynamic Endoscopic Scene Simulations via MLLM-Guided Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Posits that the availability of calibrated, synchronized viewpoints provides sufficient spatial consistency, and therefore, explicit temporal coupling, or complex multi-body constraints seems unnecessary for retrospective NVS.
To this end, the paper proposes an approach tailored for synchronized MV dynamic scene.

By initializing the SfM-derived point cloud at the start time and propagating optimized Gaussians over time, the method shows that efficient retrospective NVS can be achieved without imposing a temporal deformation constraint.
papers.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Retrospective Dynamic Scene Novel View Synthesis with a Standardized Benchmark

key_contributions: Decomposes 4DGS into independently transmittable static-scaffold, global-deformation, and local-refinement layers whose prefixes remain renderable.
Combines Gaussian-entropy rate-distortion training, temporal mask consistency, and activation-gated capacity rollout for progressive coding.
Reports over 60% bitstream reduction at matched fidelity and about 1.7-second first-frame latency over a 2 Mbps link.
papers.title: PD-4DGS:Progressive Decomposition of 4D Gaussian Splatting for Bandwidth-Adaptive Dynamic Scene Streaming

key_contributions: Proposes CausalGS, a framework that learns the causal dynamics of complex dynamic 3D scenes solely from multi-view videos, while dispensing with the reliance on explicit priors.

At its core is an inverse physics inference module that decouples the complex dynamics problem from the video into the joint inference of two factors: the initial velocity field representing the scene's kinematics.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that CausalGS surpasses the state-of-the-art on the highly challenging task of long-term future frame extrapolation, while also exhibiting advanced performance in novel view interpolation.
papers.title: CausalGS: Learning Physical Causality of 3D Dynamic Scenes with Gaussian Representations

key_contributions: Lifts multi-view segmentation masks into coherent 3D Gaussian parts through graph clustering.
Estimates rigid part-motion priors from multi-view optical flow using differential evolution to warm-start per-timestep optimization.
Combines adaptive iteration counts, learnable rigidity, and flow supervision for faster convergence, accurate tracking, and part-level editing.
papers.title: PaMoSplat: Part-Aware Motion-Guided Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Constructs scalable Gaussian levels of detail with vector quantization and corrects compression-induced color distortion using low-resolution reference images.
Implements adaptive server-client volumetric streaming by rendering references on the server and restoring color on the client.
Handles fluctuating bandwidth and generalizes across multiple Gaussian representations.
papers.title: CAGS: Color-Adaptive Volumetric Video Streaming with Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces pose-free feed-forward 4D reconstruction specialized for unstructured off-road scenes.
Uses voxel-grounded temporal Gaussian aggregation with query-conditioned temporal attention to resolve cross-timestamp conflicts.
Regularizes Gaussian geometry with surface-normal cues and reports zero-shot generalization to unseen off-road domains.
papers.title: Ground4D: Spatially-Grounded Feedforward 4D Reconstruction for Unstructured Off-Road Scenes

key_contributions: Builds a controlled baseline to isolate and analyze training heuristics that materially affect dynamic Gaussian splatting quality.
Uses duration-aware temporal partitioning plus photometric and motion discrepancies to organize dynamic primitives.
Combines gated marginalization with neural velocity fields to improve stability, reproducibility, and reconstruction quality.
papers.title: FreeTimeGS++: Secrets of Dynamic Gaussian Splatting and Their Principles

key_contributions: Evaluates dynamic monocular 3DGS models on egocentric and exocentric video using paired ego-exo recordings from the EgoExo4D dataset.
Finds that reconstruction quality is consistently lower in egocentric views.
Analysis reveals that the difference in reconstruction quality, measured in peak signal-to-noise ratio, stems from the reconstruction of static, not dynamic, content.
papers.title: Bringing a Personal Point of View: Evaluating Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces optical-flow-guided dynamic 3DGS SLAM for reconstructing static and dynamic regions.
Uses ego-motion fitting to derive category-agnostic motion masks and flow-guided camera-pose initialization.
Models dynamic Gaussian centers at keyframes with scene-flow propagation, plus temporal opacity and rotation with a Gaussian mixture model.
papers.title: Flow4DGS-SLAM: Optical Flow-Guided 4D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

key_contributions: Measures a 6.18 dB train-test PSNR gap on D-NeRF and attributes over 80% of it to Gaussian splitting while showing parameter count alone is insufficient to explain overfitting.
Combines elastic-energy deformation regularization, loss-rate-aware densification, jitter-weighted dropout, and a soft growth cap to reduce the overfitting gap by up to 57%.
papers.title: Incoherent Deformation, Not Capacity: Diagnosing and Mitigating Overfitting in Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Performs streaming optimization at clip granularity to combine local temporal consistency with long-sequence scalability.
Uses clip-specific spatiotemporal fields and residual anchor compensation for local motion modeling.
Inherits anchors and decoders between clips to reduce flicker, memory overhead, and structural drift.
papers.title: ClipGStream: Clip-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Any Length and Any Motion Multi-View Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Presents Habitat-GS, a navigation-centric embodied AI simulator extended from Habitat-Sim that integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting scene rendering and drivable gaussian avatars while maintaining full compatibility with the Habitat ecosystem.

For dynamic human modeling, the paper introduces a gaussian avatar module that enables each avatar to simultaneously serve as a photorealistic visual entity and an effective navigation obstacle, allowing agents to learn human-aware behaviors.
Experiments on point-goal navigation demonstrate that agents trained on 3DGS scenes achieve stronger cross-domain generalization, with mixed-domain training being the most effective strategy.
papers.title: Habitat-GS: A High-Fidelity Navigation Simulator with Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Defines immersive volumetric video and introduces ImViD, a synchronized multi-view audiovisual dataset covering complex indoor and outdoor dynamics.
Develops a Gaussian spatiotemporal reconstruction pipeline with flow-guided initialization, temporal camera calibration, and joint supervision.
Adds sound-field reconstruction and evaluates temporally stable audiovisual playback across large six-degree-of-freedom viewing regions.
papers.title: Realizing Immersive Volumetric Video: A Multimodal Framework for 6-DoF VR Engagement

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper proposes GEAR, an EM-style alternating optimization framework that jointly models geometry and motion as interdependent components within a Gaussian Splatting representation.

To enhance part segmentation quality without sacrificing generalization, the method leverages a vanilla 2D segmentation model to provide multi-view part priors, and employ a weakly supervised constraint to regularize the latent variable.

Experiments on multiple benchmarks and the newly constructed dataset GEAR-Multi demonstrate that GEAR achieves state-of-the-art results in geometric reconstruction and motion parameters estimation, particularly on complex articulated objects with multiple movable parts.
papers.title: GEAR: GEometry-motion Alternating Refinement for Articulated Object Modeling with Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces GS-Surrogate, a deformable Gaussian Splatting-based visualization surrogate for parameter-space exploration.
The method first constructs a canonical Gaussian field as a base 3D representation and adapts it through sequential parameter-conditioned deformations.

By separating simulation-related variations from visualization-specific changes, this explicit formulation enables efficient and controllable adaptation to different visualization tasks, such as isosurface extraction and transfer function editing.
papers.title: GS-Surrogate: Deformable Gaussian Splatting for Parameter Space Exploration of Ensemble Simulations

key_contributions: Introduces PanopticQuery, a framework for unified query-time reasoning in 4D scenes.
Experiments demonstrate that PanopticQuery sets a new state of the art on complex language queries, effectively handling attributes, actions, spatial relationships, and multi-object interactions.

The approach builds on 4D Gaussian Splatting for high-fidelity dynamic reconstruction and introduces a multi-view semantic consensus mechanism that grounds natural language queries by aggregating 2D semantic predictions across multiple views and time frames.
papers.title: PanopticQuery: Unified Query-Time Reasoning for 4D Scenes

key_contributions: Generates a dynamic Gaussian avatar from a single portrait with a decoder-only autoregressive Transformer that emits an adaptive point cloud.
Jointly predicts per-point binding information for animation, then decodes complete Gaussian attributes from the generated points.
Conditions the Gaussian decoder on autoregressive latent features to improve avatar fidelity.
papers.title: AvatarPointillist: AutoRegressive 4D Gaussian Avatarization

key_contributions: Targets high-fidelity 4D Gaussian reconstruction from video captured by as few as four portable cameras.
Introduces a neural decaying function on Gaussian opacities to focus 4DGS gradients more strongly on geometry learning.
Addresses the geometry-versus-appearance learning imbalance in sparse-camera settings.
papers.title: 4C4D: 4 Camera 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Models human and object motion with separate representations suited to articulated bodies and rigid-object trajectories.
Combines HexPlane human features with cubic Hermite spline object features through interaction-aware cross-attention.
Improves reconstruction around occlusion, contact, and manipulation where independently modeled actors become inconsistent.
papers.title: HOIGS: Human-Object Interaction Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Integrates Gaussian processes with 4DGS to quantify motion uncertainty and estimate motion in occluded or sparsely observed regions.
Supports temporal extrapolation beyond observed frames through probabilistic deformation modeling.
Introduces spatiotemporal deformation kernels and variational inference with inducing points to make Gaussian-process inference tractable.
papers.title: GP-4DGS: Probabilistic 4D Gaussian Splatting from Monocular Video via Variational Gaussian Processes

key_contributions: Uses off-the-shelf point tracking to improve dynamic 3D Gaussian reconstruction under large inter-frame displacements.
Triangulates per-view pixel trajectories onto Gaussians to guide their relocation, rotation, and scale before optimization.
Enables parallel processing of adjacent frames while aiming to preserve rendering quality.
papers.title: TrackerSplat: Exploiting Point Tracking for Fast and Robust Dynamic 3D Gaussians Reconstruction

key_contributions: Learns instance-consistent and language-aligned Gaussian features from temporally aligned masks and multimodal-language-model sentence embeddings.
Uses optical flow to bridge 2D and 4D motion, improving dynamic Gaussian initialization and reducing temporal drift.
Adds geometry-aware SDF and surface-continuity constraints for coherent reconstruction, instance segmentation, and open-vocabulary querying.
papers.title: Director: Instance-aware Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Modeling and Understanding

key_contributions: Models per-primitive motion with coupled SE(3) transformations instead of fragmented piecewise-linear trajectories.
Adds hierarchical Bézier residuals and learnable local anchors to represent complex nonlinear rigid-body motion.
Preserves temporal identity and limits Gaussian proliferation over 600–1200-frame sequences.
papers.title: TRiGS: Temporal Rigid-Body Motion for Scalable 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces a scalable motion field based on cluster-centric basis transformations that expand to model evolving motion patterns.
Uses progressive background extension to incorporate newly visible regions, refine camera poses, and model transient shadows.
Adds foreground propagation with staged refinement to enforce motion consistency over large scenes and extended sequences.
papers.title: MotionScale: Reconstructing Appearance, Geometry, and Motion of Dynamic Scenes with Scalable 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Reconstructs dynamic Gaussian scenes from monocular video with explicit continuous motion.
Models continuous Gaussian position and orientation deformation with compact SE(3) B-spline motion bases.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in novel view synthesis.
papers.title: Learning Explicit Continuous Motion Representation for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from Monocular Videos

key_contributions: To address this, the paper proposes MoRGS, an efficient online per-Gaussian motion reasoning framework that explicitly models per-Gaussian motion to improve 4D reconstruction quality.
Specifically, the method leverages optical flow on a sparse set of key views as lightweight motion cues that regularize per-Gaussian motion beyond photometric supervision.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that MoRGS achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and motion fidelity among online methods, while maintaining streamable performance.
papers.title: MoRGS: Efficient Per-Gaussian Motion Reasoning for Streamable Dynamic 3D Scenes

key_contributions: Proposes a novel method to explicitly preserve the local geometric structure of Gaussians across time in 4D scenes.
The core idea is to introduce a view-space ray grouping strategy that clusters Gaussians intersected by the same ray, considering only those whose -blending weights exceed a threshold.
Demonstrates the efficacy of the method by integrating it into two distinct baseline models.
papers.title: Relaxed Rigidity with Ray-based Grouping for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To overcome these limitations, the paper presents FRoG, an efficient and robust framework for high-quality dynamic scene reconstruction.
These methods maintain 3D Gaussian attributes in a canonical field and employ the deformation field to transform this field across temporal sequences.
FRoG integrates per-Gaussian embedding with a coarse-to-fine temporal embedding strategy, accelerating rendering through the early fusion of temporal embeddings.
papers.title: Fast and Robust Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Presents Inst4DGS, an instance-decomposed 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approach with long-horizon per-Gaussian trajectories.
To further improve efficiency, the paper proposes instance-decomposed motion scaffolds that provide low-dimensional motion bases per object for long-horizon trajectory optimization.
Experiments on Panoptic Studio and Neural3DV show that Inst4DGS jointly supports tracking and instance decomposition while achieving state-of-the-art rendering and segmentation quality.
papers.title: Inst4DGS: Instance-Decomposed 4D Gaussian Splatting with Multi-Video Label Permutation Learning

key_contributions: Presents AHOY, a method for reconstructing complete, animatable 3D Gaussian avatars from in-the-wild monocular video despite heavy occlusion.
Uses identity-finetuned diffusion to supervise occluded body regions and a two-stage canonical-to-pose architecture for sparse observations.
Reconstructing from such footage poses fundamental challenges: large body regions may never be observed, and multi-view supervision per pose is unavailable.
papers.title: AHOY! Animatable Humans under Occlusion from YouTube Videos with Gaussian Splatting and Video Diffusion Priors

key_contributions: Holds Instant Gaussian Stream fixed and sweeps five anchor samplers across budgets and refinement settings on N3DV and MeetingRoom.
Finds random or uniform sampling with 4,096 anchors matches farthest-point sampling with 8,192 anchors within measurement error and releases the sweep as a sampler benchmark.
papers.title: Does it matter which Gaussians you pick in 4D Gaussian streaming?

key_contributions: To this end, the paper proposes ProgressiveAvatars, a progressive avatar representation built on a hierarchy of 3D Gaussians grown by adaptive implicit subdivision on a template mesh. 3D Gaussians are defined in face-local coordinates.
The hierarchy expands when screen-space signals indicate a lack of detail, allocating resources to important areas.

Leveraging importance ranking, ProgressiveAvatars supports incremental loading and rendering, adding new Gaussians as they arrive while preserving previous content, thus achieving smooth quality improvements across varying bandwidths.
papers.title: ProgressiveAvatars: Progressive Animatable 3D Gaussian Avatars

key_contributions: Proposes 4D Synchronized Fields, a 4D Gaussian representation that learns object-factored motion in-loop during reconstruction and synchronizes language to the resulting kinematics through a per-object conditioned field.

Each Gaussian trajectory is decomposed into shared object motion plus an implicit residual, and a kinematic-conditioned ridge map predicts temporal semantic variation, yielding a single representation in which reconstruction, motion, and semantics are structurally coupled.
On HyperNeRF, 4D Synchronized Fields achieves 28.52 dB mean PSNR, the highest among all language-grounded and motion-aware baselines, within 1.5 dB of reconstruction-only methods.
papers.title: 4D Synchronized Fields: Motion-Language Gaussian Splatting for Temporal Scene Understanding

key_contributions: Defines temporal behavior of 3D Gaussians explicitly to mitigate temporal aliasing in continuous-time rendering.
Combines optical-flow-guided initialization and supervision with triple-rendering supervision for smooth interpolation.
Targets ghost-free, temporally coherent rendering between observed timestamps.
papers.title: RetimeGS: Continuous-Time Reconstruction of 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To address this, the paper presents Mango-GS, a multi-frame, node-guided framework for high-fidelity 4D reconstruction.
The framework is trained end-to-end, enhanced by an input masking strategy and two multi-frame losses to improve robustness.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that Mango-GS achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and real-time rendering speed, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction and interactive rendering of dynamic scenes.
papers.title: Mango-GS: Enhancing Spatio-Temporal Consistency in Dynamic Scenes Reconstruction using Multi-Frame Node-Guided 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Adapts the VGGT 3D foundation model to generate 4D Gaussian scene representations for driving scenes in a forward pass.
Uses hybrid Gaussian prediction heads that separate spatial-coordinate regression from appearance prediction.
Represents dynamic environments through static-dynamic composition with velocity modeling.
papers.title: ReconDrive: Fast Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Splatting for Autonomous Driving Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces a Galilean-shearing formulation that separates Gaussian velocity from spatial covariance instead of entangling motion with geometry.
Models motion explicitly while preserving a geometrically interpretable canonical Gaussian representation.
Adds a context- and velocity-conditioned deformation network to refine Gaussian shape and orientation for complex dynamics.
papers.title: Decoupling Motion and Geometry in 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Reconstructs a dense explicit 4D representation from two unposed images in a unified feed-forward framework.
Jointly estimates dynamic Gaussian geometry, 3D motion, and camera pose.
Renders multiple signals from shared Gaussians, coupling appearance, depth, and motion for self-supervised image-synthesis training.
papers.title: UFO-4D: Unposed Feedforward 4D Reconstruction from Two Images

key_contributions: Maps Gaussian attributes into structured multi-scale UV atlases for compact, image-native storage compatible with conventional video codecs.
Uses flow-guided Gaussian labeling and video keyframing to stabilize static regions and maintain temporal coherence under large motion and disocclusion.
Introduces PackUV-2B, a 100-sequence, two-billion-frame multi-view dataset, and demonstrates consistent reconstruction on videos up to 30 minutes.
papers.title: PackUV: Packed Gaussian UV Maps for 4D Volumetric Video

key_contributions: Introduces monocular geometry lifting to recover static and dynamic geometry from a single UAV sequence.
Adds differentiable ground-support, upright-stability, and trajectory-smoothness priors for physically consistent motion.
Provides a real-world UAV dataset for evaluating dynamic aerial reconstruction.
papers.title: AeroDGS: Physically Consistent Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Single-Sequence Aerial 4D Reconstruction

key_contributions: Presents Motion Group-aware Gaussian Forecasting (MoGaF), a framework for long-term scene extrapolation built upon the 4D Gaussian Splatting representation.
Leveraging this structured space-time representation, a lightweight forecasting module predicts future motion, enabling realistic and temporally stable scene evolution.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that MoGaF consistently outperforms existing baselines in rendering quality, motion plausibility, and long-term forecasting stability.
papers.title: Space-Time Forecasting of Dynamic Scenes with Motion-aware Gaussian Grouping

key_contributions: Introduces a 4D-aware Gaussian-splatting SLAM framework with uncertainty-aware perception of scene changes.
Integrates motion-blur rendering and extends per-pixel uncertainty modeling to blurred dynamic inputs.
Uses semantic-guided uncertainty reweighting and learnable opacity weights for adaptive 4D mapping.
papers.title: RU4D-SLAM: Reweighting Uncertainty in Gaussian Splatting SLAM for 4D Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Presents an efficient learning-free 4D Gaussian segmentation framework that lifts video segmentation masks to 4D spaces, whose core is a two-stage iterative boundary refinement, TIBR4D.
Furthermore, a temporal segmentation merging strategy is proposed for IGIT to balance identity consistency and dynamic awareness.
Experiments on HyperNeRF and Neu3D demonstrate that the method produces accurate object Gaussian point clouds with clearer boundaries and higher efficiency compared to SOTA methods.
papers.title: TIBR4D: Tracing-Guided Iterative Boundary Refinement for Efficient 4D Gaussian Segmentation

key_contributions: Formulates occluded monocular human rendering as maximum a posteriori estimation under heteroscedastic observation noise.
Combines a probabilistic deformation network with joint rasterization to render uncertainty maps that modulate unreliable image gradients.
Uses confidence-aware regularization to prevent geometric drift where visual evidence is unreliable.
papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Monocular Occluded Human Rendering

key_contributions: Proposes Constrained Dynamic Gaussian Splatting (CDGS), a novel framework that formulates dynamic scene reconstruction as a budget-constrained optimization problem to enforce a strict, user-defined Gaussian budget during training.
Furthermore, the method implements a three-phase training strategy to seamlessly integrate these constraints, ensuring precise adherence to the target count.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that CDGS delivers optimal rendering quality under varying capacity limits, achieving over 3x compression compared to state-of-the-art methods.
papers.title: Constrained Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces a learnable flat-top lifespan that gives each Gaussian an explicit interval of temporal influence.
Modulates motion by lifespan so long-lived static content remains stable while short-lived primitives capture dynamics.
Uses lifespan- and velocity-aware densification to sharpen reconstruction while retaining high-resolution real-time rendering.
papers.title: SharpTimeGS: Sharp and Stable Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Lifespan Modulation

key_contributions: Presents VRGaussianAvatar, an integrated system that enables real-time full-body 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) avatars in virtual reality using only head-mounted display (HMD) tracking signals.

To improve stereo rendering efficiency, the paper introduces Binocular Batching, which jointly processes left and right eye views in a single batched pass to reduce redundant computation and support high-resolution VR displays.
Results show that VRGaussianAvatar sustains interactive VR performance and yields higher perceived appearance similarity, embodiment, and plausibility.
papers.title: VRGaussianAvatar: Integrating 3D Gaussian Avatars into VR

key_contributions: Uses a hierarchical point-based latent representation with per-Gaussian support and local aggregation to avoid empty-space redundancy.
Compresses both temporal latent features and inter-frame neural-network parameters in a unified end-to-end framework.
Reports a 67 percent storage reduction against its baseline while maintaining high reconstruction fidelity.
papers.title: HPC: Hierarchical Point-based Latent Representation for Streaming Dynamic Gaussian Splatting Compression

key_contributions: To address these issues, the paper introduces Neural Gaussian Force Field (NGFF), an end-to-end neural framework that integrates 3D Gaussian perception with physics-based dynamic modeling to generate interactive, physically realistic 4D videos from multi-view RGB.
Evaluations on synthetic and real 3D scenarios show NGFF's strong generalization and robustness in physical reasoning, advancing video prediction towards physics-grounded world models.

To support training, the method presents GSCollision, a 4D Gaussian dataset featuring diverse materials, multi-object interactions, and complex scenes, totaling over 640k rendered physical videos ( 4 TB).
papers.title: Learning Physics-Grounded 4D Dynamics with Neural Gaussian Force Fields

key_contributions: Models data uncertainty in Gaussian splatting with a probabilistic graphical framework.
Extends 4D Gaussian splatting to account for multiple types of data uncertainty.

Being the new paradigm of neural rendering, Gaussian Splatting has been investigated in many applications, with the main effort in extending its representation, improving its optimization process, and accelerating its speed.
papers.title: Graphical X Splatting (GraphiXS): A Graphical Model for 4D Gaussian Splatting under Uncertainty

key_contributions: To bridge this gap, the paper proposes StreamLoD-GS, an LoD-based Gaussian Splatting framework designed specifically for SFVV.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that StreamLoD-GS achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance in terms of quality, efficiency, and storage.

The approach integrates three core innovations: 1) an Anchor- and Octree-based LoD-structured 3DGS with a hierarchical Gaussian dropout technique to ensure efficient and stable optimization while maintaining high-quality rendering; 2) a GMM-based motion partitioning mechanism.
papers.title: LoD-Structured 3D Gaussian Splatting for Streaming Video Reconstruction

key_contributions: To tackle this issue, this study proposes the GS-DMSR method.

Additionally, this research integrates a multi-scale manifold enhancement module, which leverages the collaborative optimization of an implicit nonlinear decoder and an explicit deformation field to enhance the modeling efficiency for complex deformation scenes.
Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves a frame rate of up to 96 FPS on synthetic datasets, while effectively reducing both storage overhead and training time.
papers.title: GS-DMSR: Dynamic Sensitive Multi-scale Manifold Enhancement for Accelerated High-Quality 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Presents a method for consistent lighting and shadows when animated 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) avatars interact with 3DGS scenes or with dynamic objects inserted into otherwise static scenes.
Demonstrates environment consistent lighting for avatars from AvatarX and ActorsHQ, composited into ScanNet++, DL3DV, and SuperSplat scenes, and show interactions with inserted objects.
The key contribution is Deep Gaussian Shadow Maps (DGSM), a modern analogue of the classical shadow mapping algorithm tailored to the volumetric 3DGS representation.
papers.title: Animated 3DGS Avatars in Diverse Scenes with Consistent Lighting and Shadows

key_contributions: Pose-free feed-forward 4DGS reconstructs monocular videos with bidirectional linear and angular Gaussian motion.
Online Gaussian degradation simulation couples reconstructed novel-view conditions to a video diffusion model without offline data preprocessing.
The reconstruction-generation pipeline supports novel trajectories, editing, tracking, stabilization, and other 4D world applications.
papers.title: NeoVerse: Enhancing 4D World Model with in-the-wild Monocular Videos

key_contributions: Presents SV-GS, a framework that simultaneously estimates a deformation model and the object's motion over time under sparse observations.
Uses a rough skeleton graph and an initial static reconstruction to guide motion estimation under sparse observations.
Improves PSNR by up to 34% on synthetic sparse-view data and matches dense monocular-video methods on real data.
papers.title: SV-GS: Sparse View 4D Reconstruction with Skeleton-Driven Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: This paper presents an effective solution for view extrapolation in autonomous driving scenarios.
Employs a deformable 4D Gaussian framework to reconstruct the scene.
With only images and optional camera poses, the method firsts estimate a global static point cloud and per-frame dynamic point clouds, fusing them into a unified representation.
papers.title: DriveExplorer: Images-Only Decoupled 4D Reconstruction with Progressive Restoration for Driving View Extrapolation

key_contributions: Formulates the view selection problem as an active learning problem, where the goal is to prioritize frames that provide the greatest information gain for model training.

To this end, the paper proposes an active learning algorithm with Fisher Information that quantifies the informativeness of candidate views with respect to both semantic Gaussian parameters and deformation networks.

Experimental results demonstrate that the approach consistently improves rendering quality and semantic segmentation performance, outperforming baseline methods based on random selection and uncertainty-based heuristics.
papers.title: Next Best View Selections for Semantic and Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Converts Gaussian video streams into multi-channel 2D formats and selects key frames to stabilize long-sequence reconstruction.
Combines temporal coherence with an inflation loss to reduce training time and representation size.
Formulates delivery as integer linear programming and selects pruning levels online to balance reconstruction quality against bandwidth.
papers.title: AirGS: Real-Time 4D Gaussian Streaming for Free-Viewpoint Video Experiences

key_contributions: Experiments on dynamic scene benchmarks show that EvoGS achieves better motion coherence and temporal consistency compared to deformation-field baselines while maintaining real-time rendering.
Reinterprets 4D Gaussian Splatting as a continuous-time dynamical system, where scene motion arises from integrating a learned neural dynamical field rather than applying per-frame deformations.
This formulation, which the method calls EvoGS, treats the Gaussian representation as an evolving physical system whose state evolves continuously under a learned motion law.
papers.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting as a Learned Dynamical System

key_contributions: To obtain a more efficient model with fewer redundant parameters, in this paper, the paper proposes Hybrid Gaussian Splatting (HGS), a compact and efficient framework explicitly designed to disentangle static and dynamic regions.
The core innovation of HGS lies in the Static-Dynamic Decomposition (SDD) strategy, which leverages Radial Basis Function (RBF) modeling for Gaussian primitives.
Experimental results demonstrate that the method reduces model size by up to 98% and achieves real-time rendering at up to 125 FPS at 4K resolution on a single RTX 3090 GPU.
papers.title: HGS: Hybrid Gaussian Splatting with Static-Dynamic Decomposition for Compact Dynamic View Synthesis

key_contributions: Introduces a fully automatic pipeline for dynamic scene reconstruction from casually captured monocular RGB videos.
Rather than designing a new scene representation, the method enhances the priors that drive Dynamic Gaussian Splatting.
Uses video segmentation and epipolar error to preserve thin structures, supervise object depth, and support skeleton sampling and mask-guided re-identification.
papers.title: Prior-Enhanced Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction from Casual Video

key_contributions: Introduces NeHaD, a neural deformation field for dynamic Gaussian Splatting governed by Hamiltonian mechanics.
Employs Hamiltonian neural networks to implicitly learn underlying physical laws governing deformation.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that NeHaD achieves physically plausible results with a rendering quality-efficiency trade-off.
papers.title: Neural Hamiltonian Deformation Fields for Dynamic Scene Rendering

key_contributions: D²GSLAM jointly performs dynamic-scene reconstruction and camera tracking with a Gaussian scene representation.
The system is composed of four key components: (i) the paper proposes a geometric-prompt dynamic separation method to distinguish between static and dynamic elements of the scene.
This approach leverages the geometric consistency of Gaussian representation and scene geometry to obtain coarse dynamic regions.
papers.title: D²GSLAM: 4D Dynamic Gaussian Splatting SLAM

key_contributions: Progressively constructs local key-frame anchor spaces from a globally consistent canonical anchor.
Learns bidirectional deformations and opacity blending between neighboring anchors to suppress boundary flicker.
Uses feature-variance-guided hierarchical densification while maintaining bounded memory and random temporal access.
papers.title: MoRel: Long-Range Flicker-Free 4D Motion Modeling via Anchor Relay-based Bidirectional Blending with Hierarchical Densification

key_contributions: Binds 2D Gaussian primitives to UV-mapped patches on a template mesh, linking splatting with conventional texture editing.
Learns continuous material textures and physically based appearance for relighting under new illumination.
Supports texture edits and relighting without reoptimizing the full avatar representation.
papers.title: GTAvatar: Bridging Gaussian Splatting and Texture Mapping for Relightable and Editable Gaussian Avatars

key_contributions: Provides a unified survey of compact and efficient Gaussian splatting methods for both static 3D and dynamic 4D scenes.
Organizes prior work into parameter-compression and representation-restructuring approaches.
Summarizes datasets, metrics, benchmark comparisons, limitations, and research directions for scalable Gaussian representations.
papers.title: SUCCESS-GS: Survey of Compactness and Compression for Efficient Static and Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To address this, the paper presents TED-4DGS, a temporally activated and embedding-based deformation scheme for rate-distortion-optimized 4DGS compression that unifies the strengths of both families.
TED-4DGS is built on a sparse anchor-based 3DGS representation.

Each canonical anchor is assigned learnable temporal-activation parameters to specify its appearance and disappearance transitions over time, while a lightweight per-anchor temporal embedding queries a shared deformation bank to produce anchor-specific deformation.
papers.title: TED-4DGS: Temporally Activated and Embedding-based Deformation for 4DGS Compression

key_contributions: To achieve this, the paper introduces a novel application of dynamic Gaussian splatting: the scene is modeled dynamically, which retains nearby temporal variation, and a static scene is rendered by fixing the model's time parameter.
Proposes Splannequin, an architecture-agnostic regularization that detects two states of Gaussian primitives, hidden and defective, and applies temporal anchoring.
Under predominantly forward camera motion, hidden states are anchored to their recent well-observed past states, while defective states are anchored to future states with stronger supervision.
papers.title: Splannequin: Freezing Monocular Mannequin-Challenge Footage with Dual-Detection Splatting

key_contributions: Presents a novel multi-video 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approach designed to handle real-world, unsynchronized video sets.
The approach, SyncTrack4D, directly leverages dense 4D track representation of dynamic scene parts as cues for simultaneous cross-video synchronization and 4DGS reconstruction.
Firsts compute dense per-video 4D feature tracks and cross-video track correspondences by Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport approach.
papers.title: SyncTrack4D: Cross-Video Motion Alignment and Video Synchronization for Multi-Video 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Presents Motion4D, a novel framework that addresses these challenges by integrating 2D priors from foundation models into a unified 4D Gaussian Splatting representation.
Alternates sequential motion and semantic updates with global joint refinement for local and long-term consistency.

Extensive evaluations demonstrate that the Motion4D significantly outperforms both 2D foundation models and existing 3D-based approaches across diverse scene understanding tasks, including point-based tracking, video object segmentation, and novel view synthesis.
papers.title: Motion4D: Learning 3D-Consistent Motion and Semantics for 4D Scene Understanding

key_contributions: Reformulates camera pose as a model output for pose-free, single-pass driving-scene reconstruction from sparse images.
Jointly predicts per-frame Gaussian maps and camera parameters, with dynamic and lifespan heads for motion and temporal visibility.
Uses diffusion-based rendering refinement to reduce motion and interpolation artifacts.
papers.title: DGGT: Feedforward 4D Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes using Unposed Images

key_contributions: To address this, the paper proposes a topology-aware dynamic reconstruction framework based on Gaussian Splatting.
Introduces a Gaussian topological structure that explicitly encodes spatial connectivity.
Experimental results demonstrate that the method reconstructs topology-consistent mesh sequences with significantly higher accuracy than existing approaches.
papers.title: TagSplat: Topology-Aware Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Mesh Modeling and Tracking

key_contributions: Introduces Dynamic-eDiTor, a training-free text-driven 4D editing framework leveraging Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) and 4DGS.
Extensive experiments on multi-view video dataset DyNeRF demonstrate that the method achieves superior editing fidelity and both multi-view and temporal consistency prior approaches.

This mechanism consists of Spatio-Temporal Sub-Grid Attention (STGA) for locally consistent cross-view and temporal fusion, and Context Token Propagation (CTP) for global propagation via token inheritance and optical-flow-guided token replacement.
papers.title: Dynamic-eDiTor: Training-Free Text-Driven 4D Scene Editing with Multimodal Diffusion Transformer

key_contributions: Proposes Cross-Temporal 3D Gaussian Splatting (Cross-Temporal 3DGS), a novel framework for efficiently reconstructing and updating 3D scenes across different time periods, using sparse images and previously captured scene priors.

The method supports non-continuous capture, enabling not only updates using new sparse views to refine existing scenes, but also recovering past scenes from limited data with the help of current captures.

Experimental results show significant improvements over baseline methods in reconstruction quality and data efficiency, making this approach a promising solution for scene versioning, cross-temporal digital twins, and long-term spatial documentation.
papers.title: Cross-Temporal 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Guided Scene Update

key_contributions: To overcome these challenges, the paper proposes TGSFormer, a scalable Temporal Gaussian Splatting framework for embodied SSC.
Subsequently, a Confidence-aware Voxel Fusion module merges overlapping primitives into voxel-aligned representations, regulating density and maintaining compactness.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that TGSFormer achieves state-of-the-art results on both local and embodied SSC benchmarks, offering superior accuracy and scalability with significantly fewer primitives while maintaining consistent long-term scene integrity.
papers.title: TGSFormer: Scalable Temporal Gaussian Splatting for Embodied Semantic Scene Completion

key_contributions: Detects dynamically inconsistent multi-view-stereo estimates before they corrupt sparse-input 4D reconstruction.
Regularizes geometry with global and local depth constraints derived from monocular depth predictions.
Improves temporal and cross-view geometric consistency when only a small number of input cameras are available.
papers.title: Geometry-Consistent 4D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-Input Dynamic View Synthesis

key_contributions: Presents a unique system for large-scale, multi-performer, high resolution 4D volumetric capture providing realistic free-viewpoint video up to and including 4K resolution facial closeups.
To achieve this, the method employs a novel volumetric capture, reconstruction and rendering pipeline based on Dynamic Gaussian Splatting and Diffusion-based Detail Enhancement.
Designs the pipeline specifically to meet the demands of high-end media production.
papers.title: Detail Enhanced Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Volumetric Capture

key_contributions: Endo-G²T combines geometry-guided supervision with temporally aware training for time-embedded 4DGS.

First, geo-guided prior distillation converts confidence-gated monocular depth into supervision with scale-invariant depth and depth-gradient losses, using a warm-up-to-cap schedule to inject priors softly and avoid early overfitting.

Second, a time-embedded Gaussian field represents dynamics in XYZT with a rotor-like rotation parameterization, yielding temporally coherent geometry with lightweight regularization that favors smooth motion and crisp opacity boundaries.
papers.title: Endo-G²T: Geometry-Guided & Temporally Aware Time-Embedded 4DGS For Endoscopic Scenes

key_contributions: To this end, the paper introduces Neural Texture Splatting (NTS).
Extensive experiments show that Neural Texture Splatting consistently improves models and achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks.
At the core of the approach is a global neural field (represented as a hybrid of a tri-plane and a neural decoder) that predicts local appearance and geometric fields for each primitive.
papers.title: Neural Texture Splatting: Expressive 3D Gaussian Splatting for View Synthesis, Geometry, and Dynamic Reconstruction

key_contributions: Derives a maximum sampling-frequency formulation for 4D Gaussian Splatting.
Introduces a 4D scale-adaptive filter and scale loss to regulate sampling frequency across rendering scales.
Reduces high-frequency artifacts and redundant Gaussians in monocular and multi-view video reconstruction.
papers.title: Alias-free 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Addresses these issues by introducing a novel method composed of two key components: (1) Elliptical Error Clustering and Error Correcting Splat Addition that pinpoints dynamic areas to improve and initialize fitting splats, and (2) Grouped.

Specifically, the method classifies rendering errors into missing-color and occlusion types, then apply targeted corrections via backprojection or foreground splitting guided by cross-view color consistency.
Improves PSNR by 0.39 dB on Technicolor Light Field while improving temporal consistency.
papers.title: Clustered Error Correction with Grouped 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces a structured Gaussian representation specialized for jointly reconstructing deforming hands and manipulated objects.
Conditions object deformation on hand motion to capture interaction rather than optimizing the two actors independently.
Uses progressive static-to-dynamic optimization with physical and illumination regularization for stable reconstruction.
papers.title: Interaction-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction

key_contributions: To address this challenge, a novel temporal alignment strategy is proposed for high-quality 4DGS reconstruction from unsynchronized multi-view videos.
Experiments show that the approach effectively processes temporally misaligned videos and significantly enhances baseline methods.
The method features a coarse-to-fine alignment module that estimates and compensates for each camera's time shift.
papers.title: Dynamic Gaussian Scene Reconstruction from Unsynchronized Videos

key_contributions: Presents a novel framework for animating humans in 3D scenes using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), a neural scene representation that has recently achieved state-of-the-art photorealistic results for novel-view synthesis but remains under-explored for human-scene animation.

Central to the method is a Gaussian-aligned motion module that synthesizes motion without explicit scene geometry, using opacity-based cues and projected Gaussian structures to guide human placement and pose alignment.

Unlike existing animation pipelines that use meshes or point clouds as the underlying 3D representation, the approach introduces the use of 3DGS as the 3D representation for animating humans in scenes.
papers.title: AHA! Animating Human Avatars in Diverse Scenes with Gaussian Splatting
