key_contributions: Targets dynamic reconstruction from temporally sparse frames, where large gaps make deformation estimation underconstrained.
Aligns texture and depth cues through texture-aware deformation regularization to stabilize motion between observed frames.
Uses texture-aware canonical optimization to preserve fine appearance while filling unobserved temporal intervals.
papers.title: Sparse4DGS: 4D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-Frame Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Proposes DIAL-GS, a novel dynamic instance-aware reconstruction method for label-free street scenes with 4D Gaussian Splatting.
Guided by instance-level dynamic perception, the method employs instance-aware 4D Gaussians as the unified volumetric representation, realizing dynamic-adaptive and instance-aware reconstruction.

Experiments on urban driving scenarios show that DIAL-GS surpasses existing self-supervised baselines in reconstruction quality and instance-level editing, offering a concise yet powerful solution for urban scene modeling.
papers.title: DIAL-GS: Dynamic Instance Aware Reconstruction for Label-free Street Scenes with 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To fill this gap, the paper proposes Physics-Informed Deformable Gaussian Splatting (PIDG), which treats each Gaussian particle as a Lagrangian material point with time-varying constitutive parameters and is supervised by 2D optical flow via motion.
Specifically, the method adopts static-dynamic decoupled 4D decomposed hash encoding to reconstruct geometry and motion efficiently.

Experiments on a custom physics-driven dataset as well as on standard synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate significant gains in physical consistency and monocular dynamic reconstruction quality.
papers.title: Physics-Informed Deformable Gaussian Splatting: Towards Unified Constitutive Laws for Time-Evolving Material Field

key_contributions: Represents dynamic free-viewpoint video with canonical 3D Gaussians, temporal features, and a deformation field.
Encodes Gaussian attributes as images and temporal features as video, enabling streaming and adaptive bitrate control without retraining.
Combines sliding-window local-motion learning with transformer-guided global-motion supervision and reports an average frame size of 170 KB.
papers.title: StreamSTGS: Streaming Spatial and Temporal Gaussian Grids for Real-Time Free-Viewpoint Video

key_contributions: To address this issue, the paper introduces an approach that splits the canonical Gaussians and deformation field into foreground and background components using a sparse set of masks for frames at t=0.
Experiments on 3-D and 2.5-D entertainment datasets show that the method produces SotA qualitative and quantitative results; up to 3 PSNR higher with half the model size on 3-D scenes.
Each representation is separately trained on different loss functions during canonical pre-training.
papers.title: Splatography: Sparse multi-view dynamic Gaussian Splatting for filmmaking challenges

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper proposes SAGS, a self-adaptive alias-free Gaussian splatting framework.

Introduces an attention-driven, dynamically weighted 4D deformation decoder, leveraging 3D smoothing filters and 2D Mip filters to mitigate artifacts in deformable tissue reconstruction and better capture the fine details of tissue movement.

Experimental results on two public benchmarks, EndoNeRF and SCARED, demonstrate that the method achieves superior performance in all metrics of PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS compared to the state of the art while also delivering better.
papers.title: SAGS: Self-Adaptive Alias-Free Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Surgical Endoscopic Reconstruction

key_contributions: To address these limitations, the paper presents EndoWave, a unified spatio-temporal Gaussian Splatting framework by incorporating an optical flow-based geometric constraint and a multi-resolution rational wavelet supervision.
Second, the paper proposes a geometric constraint derived from optical flow to enhance temporal coherence and effectively constrain the 3D structure of the scene.

Extensive evaluations on two real surgical datasets, EndoNeRF and StereoMIS, demonstrate that the method EndoWave achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and visual accuracy compared to the baseline method.
papers.title: EndoWave: Rational-Wavelet 4D Gaussian Splatting for Endoscopic Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces Mono4DGS-HDR, the first system for reconstructing renderable 4D high dynamic range (HDR) scenes from unposed monocular low dynamic range (LDR) videos captured with alternating exposures.
Furthermore, the paper proposes a temporal luminance regularization strategy to enhance the temporal consistency of the HDR appearance.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that Mono4DGS-HDR significantly outperforms alternative solutions adapted from state-of-the-art methods in both rendering quality and speed.
papers.title: Mono4DGS-HDR: High Dynamic Range 4D Gaussian Splatting from Alternating-exposure Monocular Videos

key_contributions: Proposes HGC-Avatar, a novel Hierarchical Gaussian Compression framework designed for efficient transmission and high-quality rendering of dynamic avatars.

The method disentangles the Gaussian representation into a structural layer, which maps poses to Gaussians via a StyleUNet-based generator, and a motion layer, which leverages the SMPL-X model to represent temporal pose variations compactly.

Experimental results demonstrate that HGC-Avatar provides a streamable solution for rapid 3D avatar rendering, while significantly outperforming prior methods in both visual quality and compression efficiency.
papers.title: HGC-Avatar: Hierarchical Gaussian Compression for Streamable Dynamic 3D Avatars

key_contributions: To this end, the paper introduces USplat4D, a novel Uncertainty-aware dynamic Gaussian Splatting framework that propagates reliable motion cues to enhance 4D reconstruction.

Experiments on diverse real and synthetic datasets show that explicitly modeling uncertainty consistently improves dynamic Gaussian Splatting models, yielding more stable geometry under occlusion and high-quality synthesis at extreme viewpoints.
The approach estimates time-varying per-Gaussian uncertainty and leverages it to construct a spatio-temporal graph for uncertainty-aware optimization.
papers.title: Uncertainty Matters in Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Monocular 4D Reconstruction

key_contributions: This paper presents a unified framework that allows high-quality dynamic Gaussian Splatting from both defocused and motion-blurred monocular videos.

Particularly, the paper proposes to estimate per-pixel reliable blur kernels using a blur prediction network that exploits blur-related scene and camera information and is subject to a blur-aware sparsity constraint.
Extensive experiments show that the method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in generating photorealistic novel view synthesis from defocused and motion-blurred monocular videos.
papers.title: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from Defocused and Motion-blurred Monocular Videos

key_contributions: Predicts spatiotemporal Gaussian attributes from compact anchors to reduce redundant parameters across space and time.
Combines adaptive quantization with contextual entropy coding for end-to-end compression of dynamic Gaussian scenes.
Reports roughly one-megabyte representations and up to 90-fold compression on real-world sequences while preserving rendering quality.
papers.title: P-4DGS: Predictive 4D Gaussian Splatting with 90× Compression

key_contributions: This paper introduces a novel framework that jointly optimizes dynamic 3DGS from the two modalities.

Extensive experiments show that the method outperforms existing image and event-based approaches across synthetic and real scenes and prove that the method can effectively optimize dynamic 3DGS with the help of event data.
The key idea is to adopt event motion priors to guide the optimization of the deformation fields.
papers.title: DEGS: Deformable Event-based 3D Gaussian Splatting from RGB and Event Stream

key_contributions: Presents OMG4 (Optimized Minimal 4D Gaussian Splatting), a framework that constructs a compact set of salient Gaussians capable of faithfully representing 4D Gaussian models.

The method progressively prunes Gaussians in three stages: (1) Gaussian Sampling to identify primitives critical to reconstruction fidelity, (2) Gaussian Pruning to remove redundancies, and (3) Gaussian Merging to fuse primitives with similar characteristics.

Extensive experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that OMG4 significantly outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods, reducing model sizes by over 60% while maintaining reconstruction quality.
papers.title: Optimized Minimal 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Proposes a motion-adaptive framework that aligns control density with motion complexity.

To capture temporal evolution, the paper introduces spline-based trajectory parameterization initialized by 2D tracklets, replacing MLP-based deformation fields to achieve smoother motion representation and more stable optimization.

The approach achieves flexible representational density adaptation through iterative voxelization and motion tendency scoring, directly addressing the fundamental mismatch between control point allocation and motion complexity.
papers.title: From Tokens to Nodes: Semantic-Guided Motion Control for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To address these issues, the paper proposes 4DGS-Craft, a consistent and interactive 4DGS editing framework.
Enhances this model with a multi-view grid module that enforces consistency by iteratively refining multi-view input images while jointly optimizing the underlying 4D scene.
Firsts introduce a 4D-aware InstructPix2Pix model to ensure both view and temporal consistency.
papers.title: 4DGS-Craft: Consistent and Interactive 4D Gaussian Splatting Editing

key_contributions: Presents a native 4D representation for reconstructing uncalibrated casual monocular video.
Uses deep visual SLAM for geometric recovery and grid pruning to reduce representation redundancy.
Streamlines 4D Gaussian modeling to accelerate temporal reconstruction and reduce model size.
papers.title: Instant4D: 4D Gaussian Splatting in Minutes

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper proposes the Reconfigurable Continuum Gaussian Stream, dubbed ReCon-GS, a novel storage-aware framework that enables high fidelity online dynamic scene reconstruction and real-time rendering.

Specifically, the method dynamicallies allocate multi-level Anchor Gaussians in a density-adaptive fashion to capture inter-frame geometric deformations, thereby decomposing scene motion into compact coarse-to-fine representations.

Extensive experiments on three widely used datasets demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art methods, ReCon-GS improves training efficiency by approximately 15% and achieves superior FVV synthesis quality with enhanced robustness and stability.
papers.title: ReCon-GS: Continuum-Preserved Gaussian Streaming for Fast and Compact Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes

key_contributions: Introduces a feed-forward framework for generating 4D driving scenes with Gaussian-centric representations.
Uses a multimodal 4D-aware latent diffusion model to produce pixel-aligned 4D Gaussians.
Refines Gaussian-rendered novel-view videos with a video diffusion model for spatially and temporally consistent multi-track outputs.
papers.title: WorldSplat: Gaussian-Centric Feed-Forward 4D Scene Generation for Autonomous Driving

key_contributions: Recovers 3D Gaussian deformation from one target image by matching rendered Gaussian features to sparse 2D observations.
Segments and refines rigid parts to preserve geometric coherence during deformation.
Supports frame interpolation and interactive manipulation, with quantitative evaluation on DiVa-360 and Dynamic Furry Animal.
papers.title: Rigidity-Aware 3D Gaussian Deformation from a Single Image

key_contributions: To this end, the method achieves online dynamic scene reconstruction by disentangling the static and dynamic parts within a SLAM system.
The method yields novel view renderings competitive to offline methods and achieves on-par tracking with state-of-the-art dynamic SLAM methods.
The poses are tracked robustly with a novel motion masking strategy, and dynamic parts are reconstructed leveraging a progressive adaptation of a Motion Scaffolds graph.
papers.title: ProDyG: Progressive Dynamic Scene Reconstruction via Gaussian Splatting from Monocular Videos

key_contributions: Builds a perceptually weighted hierarchical 4D Gaussian representation with motion-aware grouping for progressive multi-level streaming from one bitstream.
Jointly optimizes hierarchy layers with rate-distortion supervision and attribute-specific entropy models.
Supports flexible bitrates with real-time mobile decoding and rendering while preserving temporal coherence.
papers.title: 4DGCPro: Efficient Hierarchical 4D Gaussian Compression for Progressive Volumetric Video Streaming

key_contributions: Separates static backgrounds from dynamic foregrounds with lookahead motion decomposition, reducing temporal redundancy and enabling selective streaming.
Combines a multi-resolution motion grid, shared MLP, dynamic Gaussian compensation, and adaptive background keyframes.
Jointly optimizes motion and Gaussian parameters for rate-distortion and supports background replacement and foreground-only streaming.
papers.title: 4D-MoDe: Towards Editable and Scalable Volumetric Streaming via Motion-Decoupled 4D Gaussian Compression

key_contributions: To overcome these issues, in this paper, the paper proposes a novel Spatial-Temporal Gaussian Splatting (ST-GS) framework to enhance both spatial and temporal modeling in existing Gaussian-based pipelines.
Specifically, the method develops a guidance-informed spatial aggregation strategy within a dual-mode attention mechanism to strengthen spatial interaction in Gaussian representations.

Extensive experiments on the large-scale nuScenes occupancy prediction benchmark showcase that the proposed approach not only achieves state-of-the-art performance but also delivers markedly better temporal consistency compared to existing Gaussian-based methods.
papers.title: ST-GS: Vision-Based 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction with Spatial-Temporal Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To address both the representation limitations and information scarcity, the paper proposes a novel method, FMGS-Avatar, that integrates two key innovations.

First, the paper introduces Mesh-Guided 2D Gaussian Splatting, where 2D Gaussian primitives are attached directly to template mesh faces with constrained position, rotation, and movement, enabling superior surface alignment and geometric detail preservation.

Experimental evaluation demonstrates superior reconstruction quality compared to existing methods, with notable gains in geometric accuracy and appearance fidelity while providing rich semantic information.
papers.title: FMGS-Avatar: Mesh-Guided 2D Gaussian Splatting with Foundation Model Priors for 3D Monocular Avatar Reconstruction

key_contributions: To address this bottleneck, the paper proposes 4D Gaussian Ray Tracing (4D-GRT), a novel two-stage pipeline that combines 4D Gaussian Splatting with physically-based ray tracing for camera effect simulation.
Additionally, the method constructs eight synthetic dynamic scenes in indoor environments across four camera effects as a benchmark to evaluate generated videos with camera effects.

Given multi-view videos, 4D-GRT first reconstructs dynamic scenes, then applies ray tracing to generate videos with controllable, physically accurate camera effects. 4D-GRT achieves the fastest rendering speed while performing better or comparable rendering quality compared.
papers.title: Every Camera Effect, Every Time, All at Once: 4D Gaussian Ray Tracing for Physics-based Camera Effect Data Generation

key_contributions: Presents TaoGS, a novel topology-aware dynamic Gaussian representation that disentangles motion and appearance to support, both, long-range tracking and topological adaptation.

To enable seamless integration into codec-based volumetric formats, the paper introduces a global Gaussian Lookup Table that records the lifespan of each Gaussian and organizes attributes into a lifespan-aware 2D layout.
Represents scene motion with a sparse set of motion Gaussians, which are continuously updated by a spatio-temporal tracker and photometric cues that detect structural variations across frames.
papers.title: Topology-Aware Optimization of Gaussian Primitives for Human-Centric Volumetric Videos

key_contributions: To address this issue, the paper introduces a unified optimization framework by incorporating camera poses as learnable parameters complementary to 3DGS attributes for end-to-end optimization.
Specifically, the method recasts camera and object motion as per-primitive SE(3) affine transformations on 3D Gaussians and formulate a unified optimization objective.

Extensive experiments on the Stereo Blur dataset and challenging real-world sequences demonstrate that the method achieves significant gains in reconstruction quality and pose estimation accuracy over prior dynamic deblurring methods.
papers.title: UPGS: Unified Pose-aware Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Deblurring

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper introduces Motion-Aware Partitioning of Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting (MAPo), a novel framework for high-fidelity dynamic scene reconstruction.
A common strategy involves learning a deformation field to model the temporal changes of a canonical set of 3D Gaussians.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that MAPo achieves superior rendering quality compared to baselines while maintaining comparable computational costs, particularly in regions with complex or rapid motions.
papers.title: MAPo : Motion-Aware Partitioning of Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting for High-Fidelity Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Defines a benchmark suite for standardized evaluation of 4D stylization.
Couples a base 4DGS scene representation with per-Gaussian MLPs for temporally and spatially aware appearance control.

Extensive experiments on Style4D-Bench demonstrate that Style4D achieves state-of-the-art performance in 4D stylization, producing fine-grained stylistic details with stable temporal dynamics and consistent multi-view rendering.
papers.title: Style4D-Bench: A Benchmark Suite for 4D Stylization

key_contributions: Reconstructs dynamic driving scenes in a unified neural Gaussian representation.

For static backgrounds, the paper introduces a scene-aware learnable level-of-detail (LOD) modeling strategy that explicitly accounts for near, intermediate, and far depth ranges in driving environments, enabling adaptive multi-scale Gaussian allocation.

Extensive experiments on the Waymo and KITTI benchmarks demonstrate that DriveSplat achieves state-of-the-art performance in novel-view synthesis while producing temporally stable and geometrically consistent reconstructions of dynamic driving scenes.
papers.title: DriveSplat: Unified Neural Gaussian Reconstruction for Dynamic Driving Scenes

key_contributions: Generates dynamic 3D scene representations from a single image using a feed-forward model fine-tuned from video diffusion.
Introduces 4DNeX-10M, a large-scale dataset of 4D annotations generated with reconstruction systems.
Uses a unified RGB-and-XYZ video representation and adaptation strategies for pretrained video diffusion models.
papers.title: 4DNeX: Feed-Forward 4D Generative Modeling Made Easy

key_contributions: Novel view synthesis and 4D reconstruction techniques predominantly rely on RGB cameras, thereby inheriting inherent limitations such as the dependence on adequate lighting, susceptibility to motion blur, and a limited dynamic range.

Event cameras, offering advantages of low power, high temporal resolution and high dynamic range, have brought a new perspective to addressing the scene reconstruction challenges in high-speed motion.
papers.title: E-4DGS: High-Fidelity Dynamic Reconstruction from the Multi-view Event Cameras

key_contributions: To overcome these challenges, the paper introduces Splat4D, a novel framework enabling high-fidelity 4D content generation from a monocular video.
Combines multi-view rendering, inconsistency detection, video diffusion, and asymmetric U-Net refinement for spatially and temporally coherent 4D content.
Through extensive evaluations on public benchmarks, Splat4D consistently demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across various metrics, underscoring the efficacy of the approach.
papers.title: Splat4D: Diffusion-Enhanced 4D Gaussian Splatting for Temporally and Spatially Consistent Content Creation

key_contributions: Introduces a novel approach that combines 3DGS with a motion trajectory field, enabling precise handling of complex object motions and achieving physically plausible motion trajectories.
By decoupling dynamic objects from static background, the method compactly optimizes the motion trajectory field.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that the approach achieves state-of-the-art results in both novel-view synthesis and motion trajectory recovery from monocular video, advancing the capabilities of dynamic scene reconstruction.
papers.title: 3D Gaussian Representations with Motion Trajectory Field for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper proposes a novel dynamic 3DGS framework with hybrid explicit-implicit functions.

The approach contains three key innovations: a spectral-aware Laplacian encoding architecture which merges Hash encoding and Laplacian-based module for flexible frequency motion control, an enhanced Gaussian dynamics attribute that compensates for photometric distortions caused.
Through extensive experiments, the method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in reconstructing complex dynamic scenes, achieving better reconstruction fidelity.
papers.title: Laplacian Analysis Meets Dynamics Modelling: Gaussian Splatting for 4D Reconstruction

key_contributions: This study proposes PMGS, focusing on reconstructing Projectile Motion via 3D Gaussian Splatting.

Introduces an acceleration consistency constraint to bridge Newtonian mechanics and pose estimation, and design a dynamic simulated annealing strategy that adaptively schedules learning rates based on motion states.
Experiments show PMGS's superior performance in reconstructing high-speed nonlinear rigid motion compared to mainstream dynamic methods.
papers.title: PMGS: Reconstruction of Projectile Motion Across Large Spatiotemporal Spans via 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To overcome these issues, the paper proposes a novel video diffusion-enhanced 4D Gaussian Splatting framework.

To ensure precise pose alignment and effective integration of this denoised content, the paper introduces two core innovations: a joint timestamp optimization strategy that refines interpolated frame poses, and an uncertainty distillation method that adaptively.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method significantly enhances dynamic modeling, especially for fast-moving objects, achieving an approximate PSNR gain of 2 dB for novel view synthesis over baseline approaches.
papers.title: VDEGaussian: Video Diffusion Enhanced 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Urban Scenes Modeling

key_contributions: Separates static and dynamic scene components with self-supervision, without manual annotations or precomputed masks.
Applies multiresolution 4D hash encoding to dynamic components, avoiding a plane-based low-rank assumption.
Adds spatiotemporal smoothness regularization to reduce unstable deformation artifacts.
papers.title: DASH: 4D Hash Encoding with Self-Supervised Decomposition for Real-Time Dynamic Scene Rendering

key_contributions: To tackle these challenges, the paper proposes algorithm-hardware co-design techniques.

At the algorithmic level, the paper introduces three optimizations: (1) DRAM-access reduction frustum culling to lower DRAM access overhead, (2) Adaptive tile grouping to enhance on-chip buffer reuse, and (3) Adaptive interval initialization Bucket-Bitonic sort.
At the hardware level, the paper presents a DCIM-friendly computation flow that is evaluated using the measured data from a 16nm DCIM prototype chip.
papers.title: 3DGauCIM: Accelerating Static/Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting via Digital CIM for High Frame Rate Real-Time Edge Rendering

key_contributions: Formulates dynamic Gaussian compression as end-to-end rate-distortion optimization rather than a post-processing step.
Applies a temporal wavelet transform to exploit smoothness and redundancy along explicit Gaussian trajectories.
Substantially reduces storage while retaining real-time rendering and competitive reconstruction quality.
papers.title: Temporal Smoothness-Aware Rate-Distortion Optimized 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Proposes StreamME, a method focuses on fast 3D avatar reconstruction.
This exceptionally fast training strategy, which the method refers to as on-the-fly training, is central to the approach.

The StreamME synchronously records and reconstructs a head avatar from live video streams without any pre-cached data, enabling seamless integration of the reconstructed appearance into downstream applications.
papers.title: StreamME: Simplify 3D Gaussian Avatar within Live Stream

key_contributions: To address these issues, the paper introduces an innovative framework for 3DGS volumetric video streaming.
Specifically, the method designs a 3DGS video construction method based on the Gaussian deformation field.

By employing hybrid saliency tiling and differentiated quality modeling of 3DGS video, the method achieves efficient data compression and adaptation to bandwidth fluctuations while ensuring high transmission quality.
papers.title: Adaptive 3D Gaussian Splatting Video Streaming

key_contributions: Introduces structured deformable Gaussians that organize motion and appearance for efficient dynamic-scene reconstruction.
Reduces model size and increases rendering throughput while preserving reconstruction fidelity.
Reports competitive quality with substantially lower storage and higher frame rates than prior deformable-Gaussian methods.
papers.title: SD-GS: Structured Deformable 3D Gaussians for Efficient Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Defines a standardized group-of-frames structure with I-P coding and sparse control points for extracting inter-frame motion tensors.
Combines hyperprior and spatiotemporal priors for entropy modeling with control-point-guided motion compensation and refinement.
Generalizes zero-shot across Gaussian sequences and reports more than 17-fold compression against its baseline.
papers.title: D-FCGS: Feedforward Compression of Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Free-Viewpoint Videos

key_contributions: Introduces HyperGaussians, a novel extension of 3D Gaussian Splatting for high-quality animatable face avatars.
Creating such detailed face avatars from videos is a challenging problem and has numerous applications in augmented and virtual reality.

The de facto standard, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), represents a face through a collection of 3D Gaussian primitives. 3DGS excels at rendering static faces, but the state-of-the-art still struggles with nonlinear deformations, complex lighting effects.
papers.title: HyperGaussians: High-Dimensional Gaussian Splatting for High-Fidelity Animatable Face Avatars

key_contributions: Decomposes large dynamic scenes into seed-defined local spaces to capture both large- and fine-scale motion.
Decouples shared static features from time-specific dynamic residuals and decodes them into Temporal Gaussians.
Provides adaptive static-dynamic segmentation as a by-product of local motion modeling.
papers.title: LocalDyGS: Multi-view Global Dynamic Scene Modeling via Adaptive Local Implicit Feature Decoupling

key_contributions: To address these limitations, the paper introduces a free-form deformation (FFD)-based spatial basis function and a deformation-informed framework that enforces consistency by coupling the temporal evolution of Gaussian's mean position, scale, and rotation under.
Achieves a 6× speedup over HexPlane across six CBCT datasets.
These results highlight the potential of deformation-informed 4DGS for efficient, motion-compensated CBCT reconstruction.
papers.title: DIGS: Dynamic CBCT Reconstruction using Deformation-Informed 4D Gaussian Splatting and a Low-Rank Free-Form Deformation Model

key_contributions: Introduces a position texture to subdivide the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) body model's surface and grow the human point cloud.
Adopts a strategy of point cloud decoupling and joint optimization to achieve the decoupled reconstruction of backgrounds and human bodies while preserving the interactivity of human motion.
To capture fine details of human dynamics and deformations, the method incorporates a convolutional neural network structure to predict human body point cloud features based on texture.
papers.title: SkinningGS: Editable Dynamic Human Scene Reconstruction Using Gaussian Splatting Based on a Skinning Model

key_contributions: To address this, the paper proposes Motion-aware Dynamic View Synthesis from Blurry Monocular Video via Sparse-Controlled Gaussian Splatting (DBMovi-GS), a method designed for dynamic view synthesis from blurry monocular videos.
The model generates dense 3D Gaussians, restoring sharpness from blurry videos and reconstructing detailed 3D geometry of the scene affected by dynamic motion variations.
The model achieves robust performance in novel view synthesis under dynamic blurry scenes and sets a new benchmark in realistic novel view synthesis for blurry monocular video inputs.
papers.title: DBMovi-GS: Dynamic View Synthesis from Blurry Monocular Video via Sparse-Controlled Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Proposes HoliGS, a novel deformable Gaussian splatting framework that addresses embodied view synthesis from long monocular RGB videos.

Unlike prior 4D Gaussian splatting and dynamic NeRF pipelines, which struggle with training overhead in minute-long captures, the method leverages invertible Gaussian Splatting deformation networks to reconstruct large-scale, dynamic environments accurately.

Specifically, the method decomposes each scene into a static background plus time-varying objects, each represented by learned Gaussian primitives undergoing global rigid transformations, skeleton-driven articulation, and subtle non-rigid deformations via an invertible neural flow.
papers.title: HoliGS: Holistic Gaussian Splatting for Embodied View Synthesis

key_contributions: Introduces BulletGen, an approach that takes advantage of generative models to correct errors and complete missing information in a Gaussian-based dynamic scene representation.
The method seamlessly blends generative content with both static and dynamic scene components, achieving state-of-the-art results on both novel-view synthesis, and 2D/3D tracking tasks.
This is done by aligning the output of a diffusion-based video generation model with the 4D reconstruction at a single frozen "bullet-time" step.
papers.title: BulletGen: Improving 4D Reconstruction with Bullet-Time Generation

key_contributions: Combines deformable 3DGS optimization with object-view-synthesis priors to generate multi-object 4D scenes from occluded monocular video.
To address this, GenMOJO decomposes the scene into individual objects, optimizing a differentiable set of deformable Gaussians per object.
This object-wise decomposition allows leveraging object-centric diffusion models to infer unobserved regions in novel viewpoints.
papers.title: Generative 4D Scene Gaussian Splatting with Object View-Synthesis Priors

key_contributions: Presents DynaSplat, an approach that extends Gaussian Splatting to dynamic scenes by integrating dynamic-static separation and hierarchical motion modeling.
Introduces a hierarchical motion modeling strategy that captures both coarse global transformations and fine-grained local movements, enabling accurate handling of intricate, non-rigid motions.

Extensive experiments on challenging datasets reveal that DynaSplat not only surpasses state-of-the-art alternatives in accuracy and realism but also provides a more intuitive, compact, and efficient route to dynamic scene reconstruction.
papers.title: DynaSplat: Dynamic-Static Gaussian Splatting with Hierarchical Motion Decomposition for Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: To address these limitations, the paper proposes HAIF-GS, a unified framework that enables structured and consistent dynamic modeling through sparse anchor-driven deformation.
A self-supervised Induced Flow-Guided Deformation module induces anchor motion using multi-frame feature aggregation, eliminating the need for explicit flow labels.

Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks validate that HAIF-GS significantly outperforms prior dynamic 3DGS methods in rendering quality, temporal coherence, and reconstruction efficiency.
papers.title: HAIF-GS: Hierarchical and Induced Flow-Guided Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene

key_contributions: Trains a Transformer on real-world posed monocular videos to predict 4D Gaussians in feed-forward inference.
Unifies static and dynamic components while modeling varying object lifespans in time-varying scenes.
Introduces density control and rolling-window prediction for longer space-time inputs and efficient runtime rendering.
papers.title: 4DGT: Learning a 4D Gaussian Transformer Using Real-World Monocular Videos

key_contributions: Building on DeformableGS, the paper introduces Speedy Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting (SpeeDe3DGS), which bridges this efficiency-fidelity gap through three complementary modules: Temporal Sensitivity Pruning (TSP) removes low-impact Gaussians via temporally aggregated sensitivity analysis, Temporal Sensitivity.
On the 50 dynamic scenes in MonoDyGauBench, integrating TSP and TSS into DeformableGS accelerates rendering by 6.78 on average while maintaining neural-field fidelity and using 10 fewer primitives.
Reports 13.71× faster rendering and 2.53× shorter training with GroupFlow.
papers.title: SpeeDe3DGS: Speedy Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting with Temporal Pruning and Motion Grouping

key_contributions: Introduces ODE-GS, a novel approach that integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting with latent neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs) to enable future extrapolation of dynamic 3D scenes.

Unlike existing dynamic scene reconstruction methods, which rely on time-conditioned deformation networks and are limited to interpolation within a fixed time window, ODE-GS eliminates timestamp dependency by modeling Gaussian parameter trajectories as continuous-time latent dynamics.

The approach first learns an interpolation model to generate accurate Gaussian trajectories within the observed window, then trains a Transformer encoder to aggregate past trajectories into a latent state evolved via a neural ODE.
papers.title: ODE-GS: Latent ODEs for Dynamic Scene Extrapolation with 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Allows Gaussian primitives to appear at arbitrary positions and times instead of forcing all content into a single canonical frame.
Associates each primitive with an explicit motion function plus temporal opacity and duration to model its lifespan.
Handles complex motion with fewer redundant primitives while maintaining high-quality real-time rendering.
papers.title: FreeTimeGS: Free Gaussian Primitives at Anytime and Anywhere for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces UAV4D, a framework for enabling photorealistic rendering for dynamic real-world scenes captured by UAVs.
Specifically, the method addresses the challenge of reconstructing dynamic scenes with multiple moving pedestrians from monocular video data without the need for additional sensors.
Uses a combination of a 3D foundation model and a human mesh reconstruction model to reconstruct both the scene background and humans.
papers.title: UAV4D: Dynamic Neural Rendering of Human-Centric UAV Imagery using Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces a physics-aware dynamic-view benchmark spanning 17 multi-body scenes and four material categories.
Provides synchronized multi-view imagery together with ground-truth particle trajectories and physical parameters.
Supplies evaluation and integration tooling for measuring both rendering fidelity and physical motion consistency.
papers.title: PhysGaia: A Physics-Aware Benchmark with Multi-Body Interactions for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

key_contributions: Joint online camera localization and non-rigid surface reconstruction from color and depth streams with dynamic Gaussian surface primitives.
A deformation warp field, surface regularizers, and pose optimization jointly recover geometry, appearance, dynamics, and camera motion.
Sim4D supplies synthetic ground truth and protocols for camera trajectory, geometry, and appearance evaluation.
papers.title: 4DTAM: Non-Rigid Tracking and Mapping via Dynamic Surface Gaussians

key_contributions: Presents WeatherEdit, a novel weather editing pipeline for generating realistic weather effects with controllable types and severity in 3D scenes.

For weather background editing, the paper introduces an all-in-one adapter that integrates multiple weather styles into a single pretrained diffusion model, enabling the generation of diverse weather effects in 2D image backgrounds.

Experiments on multiple driving datasets demonstrate that WeatherEdit can generate diverse weather effects with controllable condition severity, highlighting its potential for autonomous driving simulation in adverse weather.
papers.title: WeatherEdit: Controllable Weather Editing with 4D Gaussian Field

key_contributions: Proposes a novel extension to 4D Gaussian Splatting for dynamic scenes.

Then, instead of directly predicting the time-dependent signals, the method models the signal as the sum of video-constant values, segment-constant values, and frame-specific residuals, as inspired by the success of residual learning.

Demonstrates state-of-the-art visual quality and real-time rendering on several established datasets, with the greatest improvements on complex scenes with large movements, occlusions, and fine details, where current methods degrade most.
papers.title: CTRL-GS: Cascaded Temporal Residue Learning for 4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To address this limitation, the paper proposes a novel Compact Gaussian Streaming (ComGS) framework, leveraging the locality and consistency of motion in dynamic scene, that models object-consistent Gaussian point motion through keypoint-driven motion representation.
Specifically, the method firsts identify a sparse set of motion-sensitive keypoints localized within motion regions using a viewspace gradient difference strategy.
By transmitting only the keypoint attributes, this framework provides a more storage-efficient solution.
papers.title: Motion Matters: Compact Gaussian Streaming for Free-Viewpoint Video Reconstruction

key_contributions: To tackle this, the paper introduces MGStream which employs the motion-related 3D Gaussians (3DGs) to reconstruct the dynamic and the vanilla 3DGs for the static.

Extensive experiments on real-world datasets N3DV and MeetRoom demonstrate that MGStream surpasses existing streaming 3DGS-based approaches in terms of rendering quality, training/storage efficiency and temporal consistency.
The motion-related 3DGs are implemented according to the motion mask and the clustering-based convex hull algorithm.
papers.title: MGStream: Motion-aware 3D Gaussian for Streamable Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Represents static regions with 3D Gaussians and dynamic elements with 4D Gaussians.
Iteratively converts temporally invariant 4D Gaussians to 3D to reduce parameters and computation.
Preserves full 4D representations for complex dynamic motion.
papers.title: Hybrid 3D-4D Gaussian Splatting for Fast Dynamic Scene Representation

key_contributions: This work presents DLO-Splatting, an algorithm for estimating the 3D shape of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) from multi-view RGB images and gripper state information through prediction-update filtering.
The DLO-Splatting algorithm uses a position-based dynamics model with shape smoothness and rigidity dampening corrections to predict the object shape.
Optimization with a 3D Gaussian Splatting-based rendering loss iteratively renders and refines the prediction to align it with the visual observations in the update step.
papers.title: DLO-Splatting: Tracking Deformable Linear Objects Using 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Organizes dynamic Gaussians around anchors and prunes them using temporal significance to obtain a compact representation.
Uses coarse-to-fine deformation to separate anchor-level motion from local Gaussian detail.
Jointly optimizes reconstruction quality and bitrate for faster training, compact storage, and real-time rendering.
papers.title: ADC-GS: Anchor-Driven Deformable and Compressed Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Augments an anchor-based canonical representation with time-dependent feature streams that jointly decode motion and Gaussian attributes.
Uses motion-aware pruning plus temporal and spatial learned coding to exploit temporal correspondence for end-to-end compression.
Reports high-quality immersive video at 30 Mbps with real-time rendering and fast decoding.
papers.title: GIFStream: 4D Gaussian-based Immersive Video with Feature Stream

key_contributions: Proposes a method that enhances temporal consistency in online reconstruction from observations with temporal inconsistency which is inevitable in cameras.
Shows that the method restores the ideal observation by subtracting the learned error.
Demonstrates that applying the method to various baselines significantly enhances both temporal consistency and rendering quality across datasets.
papers.title: Compensating Spatiotemporally Inconsistent Observations for Online Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: To address this issue, the paper proposes HoloTime, a framework that integrates video diffusion models to generate panoramic videos from a single prompt or reference image, along with a 360-degree 4D scene reconstruction method.

Specifically, to tame video diffusion models for generating high-fidelity panoramic videos, the paper introduces the 360World dataset, the first comprehensive collection of panoramic videos suitable for downstream 4D scene reconstruction tasks.
With this curated dataset, the paper proposes Panoramic Animator, a two-stage image-to-video diffusion model that can convert panoramic images into high-quality panoramic videos.
papers.title: HoloTime: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Panoramic 4D Scene Generation

key_contributions: Decomposes a dynamic representation into compact 4D neural voxels and canonical 3D Gaussians for separate coding.
Introduces contextual coding modules for neural voxels and vector-quantized Gaussian attributes.
Reduces dynamic-scene storage while preserving rendering fidelity through learned entropy-aware compression.
papers.title: 4DGS-CC: A Contextual Coding Framework for 4D Gaussian Splatting Data Compression

key_contributions: Therefore, the paper proposes STP4D, a novel approach that aims to integrate comprehensive spatio-temporal-prompt consistency modeling for high-quality text-to-4D generation.

Specifically, STP4D employs three carefully designed modules: Time-varying Prompt Embedding, Geometric Information Enhancement, and Temporal Extension Deformation, which collaborate to accomplish this goal.
Generates a 4D asset in approximately 4.6 seconds.
papers.title: STP4D: Spatio-Temporal-Prompt Consistent Modeling for Text-to-4D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Presents MoBGS, a novel motion deblurring 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework capable of reconstructing sharp and high-quality novel spatio-temporal views from blurry monocular videos in an end-to-end manner.
In addition, the paper proposes a Latent Camera-induced Exposure Estimation (LCEE) method to ensure consistent deblurring of both a global camera and local object motions.

Extensive experiments on the Stereo Blur dataset and real-world blurry videos show that the MoBGS significantly outperforms the very recent methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance for dynamic NVS under motion blur.
papers.title: MoBGS: Motion Deblurring Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting for Blurry Monocular Video

key_contributions: Hence, the paper proposes Compressed Gaussian Splatting (CompGS++), a novel framework that leverages compact Gaussian primitives to achieve accurate 3D modeling with substantial size reduction for both static and dynamic scenes.
Specifically, the method develops a comprehensive prediction paradigm to address inter-primitive redundancy through spatial and temporal primitive prediction modules.
The design is based on the principle of eliminating redundancy both between and within primitives.
papers.title: CompGS++: Compressed Gaussian Splatting for Static and Dynamic Scene Representation

key_contributions: By involving several cutting-edge modern techniques, the paper introduces an end-to-end 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) avatar creation pipeline that leverages monocular video input to create a scalable and efficient photorealistic avatar directly compatible.

Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the preprocessing pipeline in standardizing custom data for 3DGS training and demonstrate the versatility of Gaussian avatars in Unity, highlighting the scalability and practicality of the approach.
Adds preprocessing for in-the-wild monocular video, facial-expression reconstruction, and integration with a fully rigged avatar.
papers.title: GSAC: Leveraging Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Avatar Creation with Unity Integration

key_contributions: Presents Hierarchical Motion Representation (HiMoR), a novel deformation representation for 3D Gaussian primitives capable of achieving high-quality monocular dynamic 3D reconstruction.

Proposes using a more reliable perceptual metric as an alternative, given that pixel-level metrics for evaluating monocular dynamic 3D reconstruction can sometimes fail to accurately reflect the true quality of reconstruction.
Extensive experiments demonstrate the method's efficacy in achieving superior novel view synthesis from challenging monocular videos with complex motions.
papers.title: HiMoR: Monocular Deformable Gaussian Reconstruction with Hierarchical Motion Representation

key_contributions: Proposes representing a complete 3D space for dynamic scene video by modeling explicit representations, specifically 4D Gaussians, from a single image.
The framework is focused on optimizing 3D Gaussians by generating multi-view images from a single image and creating 3D motion to optimize 4D Gaussians.
The most important part of proposed framework is consistent 3D motion estimation, which estimates common motion among multi-view images to bring the motion in 3D space closer to actual motions.
papers.title: Optimizing 4D Gaussians for Dynamic Scene Video from Single Landscape Images

key_contributions: Introduces D4DGS-SLAM, a SLAM method that uses a 4D Gaussian map representation for dynamic environments.
Uses a dynamics-aware module to estimate point dynamics, visibility, and reliability, filtering unstable points for tracking.
Applies dynamic-characteristic-dependent isotropic regularization when optimizing Gaussians.
papers.title: Embracing Dynamics: Dynamics-aware 4D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

key_contributions: Decouples temporal and spatial components of 4D Gaussians, avoiding four-dimensional matrix calculations and slicing.
Projects temporal and spatial deformations into dynamic 2D Gaussians while deferring temporal processing.
Uses a gradient-guided flow loss and temporal splitting strategy to reduce artifacts.
papers.title: Disentangled 4D Gaussian Splatting: Rendering High-Resolution Dynamic World at 343 FPS

key_contributions: Continuous-time 4D CT reconstruction deforms radiative Gaussians directly from projection sequences without phase binning.
Physiology-driven periodic consistency learns patient-specific respiratory cycles without an external gating device.
Evaluation covers 13 patients from DIR, 4DLung, and SPARE with 300 simulated projections per patient.
papers.title: X²-Gaussian: 4D Radiative Gaussian Splatting for Continuous-time Tomographic Reconstruction

key_contributions: Combines Hierarchical Gaussian Flow and Hierarchical Gaussian Guidance in a divide-and-conquer optimization.
Supports semantic 4D scene understanding on synthetic and real-world scenes.
papers.title: Divide-and-Conquer: Dual-Hierarchical Optimization for Semantic 4D Gaussian Spatting

key_contributions: Introduces a motion-aware dynamic Gaussian representation with a compact motion grid and sparse compensated Gaussians.
Jointly optimizes differentiable quantization, an implicit entropy model, and reconstruction under a rate-distortion objective.
Supports variable bitrates while exploiting inter-frame similarity and preserving large-motion details.
papers.title: 4DGC: Rate-Aware 4D Gaussian Compression for Efficient Streamable Free-Viewpoint Video

key_contributions: Introduces TaoAvatar, a lightweight full-body Gaussian talking avatar driven by facial, audio, and body-control signals.
Distills pose-dependent non-rigid deformations from a larger StyleUNet into a compact MLP and compensating blend shapes.
Supports high-fidelity real-time rendering on mobile and stereoscopic devices.
papers.title: TaoAvatar: Real-Time Lifelike Full-Body Talking Avatars for Augmented Reality via 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces an anchor-driven motion network that lifts multi-view 2D motion features into 3D and predicts target-frame Gaussian motion in one inference.
Uses refined key frames to reconstruct complex motion and limit error accumulation during streaming.
Demonstrates in-domain and cross-domain generalization with average per-frame reconstruction slightly above two seconds.
papers.title: Instant Gaussian Stream: Fast and Generalizable Streaming of Dynamic Scene Reconstruction via Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Incrementally estimates camera poses and constructs 4D Gaussian radiance fields from RGB-D image sequences.
Separates Gaussian primitives into static and dynamic sets, modeling dynamic transformations with sparse control points and an MLP.
Renders optical flow between neighboring images to supervise dynamic motion alongside photometric and geometric constraints.
papers.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

key_contributions: Identifies short-lifespan and inactive Gaussians as major temporal redundancies in 4DGS.
Introduces a spatial-temporal variation score to prune short-lifespan Gaussians.
Stores masks for active Gaussians across consecutive frames to avoid redundant rasterization computation.
papers.title: 1000+ FPS 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Rendering

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper introduces BARD-GS, a novel approach for robust dynamic scene reconstruction that effectively handles blurry inputs and imprecise camera poses.
The method comprises two main components: 1) camera motion deblurring and 2) object motion deblurring.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that BARD-GS effectively reconstructs high-quality dynamic scenes under realistic conditions, significantly outperforming existing methods.
papers.title: BARD-GS: Blur-Aware Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes via Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Prunes low-significance primitives using spatiotemporal importance to remove redundancy from dynamic Gaussian scenes.
Compresses appearance and deformation attributes with an entropy-constrained contextual model and learned hyperprior.
Maintains competitive reconstruction quality and real-time rendering with a substantially smaller representation.
papers.title: Light4GS: Lightweight Compact 4D Gaussian Splatting Generation via Context Model

key_contributions: To tackle this problem, the paper introduces DeGauss, a simple and robust self-supervised framework for dynamic scene reconstruction based on a decoupled dynamic-static Gaussian Splatting design.

Experiments on benchmarks including NeRF-on-the-go, ADT, AEA, Hot3D, and EPIC-Fields demonstrate that DeGauss consistently outperforms existing methods, establishing a strong baseline for generalizable, distractor-free 3D reconstructionin highly dynamic, interaction-rich environments.

DeGauss models dynamic elements with foreground Gaussians and static content with background Gaussians, using a probabilistic mask to coordinate their composition and enable independent yet complementary optimization.
papers.title: DeGauss: Dynamic-Static Decomposition with Gaussian Splatting for Distractor-free 3D Reconstruction

key_contributions: Learns a static-dynamic primitive decomposition and applies deformation only to dynamic Gaussians.
Uses a compact multi-resolution 4D hash mapper to transform dynamic primitives from canonical to observation space.
Reduces redundant static modeling, accelerating training and lowering storage while preserving rendering quality.
papers.title: Swift4D:Adaptive divide-and-conquer Gaussian Splatting for compact and efficient reconstruction of dynamic scene

key_contributions: To this end, the paper proposes the first real-time GS-SLAM, "DynaGSLAM'', that achieves high-quality online GS rendering, tracking, motion predictions of moving objects in dynamic scenes while jointly estimating accurate ego motion.
The DynaGSLAM outperforms SOTA static & "Anti'' dynamic GS-SLAM on three dynamic real datasets, while keeping speed and memory efficiency in practice.
Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is one of the most important environment-perception and navigation algorithms for computer vision, robotics, and autonomous cars/drones.
papers.title: DynaGSLAM: Real-Time Gaussian-Splatting SLAM for Online Rendering, Tracking, Motion Predictions of Moving Objects in Dynamic Scenes

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper proposes 4D LangSplat, which learns 4D language fields to handle time-agnostic or time-sensitive open-vocabulary queries in dynamic scenes efficiently. 4D LangSplat bypasses learning the language field from vision features.

Specifically, the paper proposes a multimodal object-wise video prompting method, consisting of visual and text prompts that guide MLLMs to generate detailed, temporally consistent, high-quality captions for objects throughout a video.

These captions are encoded using a Large Language Model into high-quality sentence embeddings, which then serve as pixel-aligned, object-specific feature supervision, facilitating open-vocabulary text queries through shared embedding spaces.
papers.title: 4D LangSplat: 4D Language Gaussian Splatting via Multimodal Large Language Models

key_contributions: Presents GASPACHO, a method for generating photorealistic, controllable renderings of human-object interactions from multi-view RGB video.

Introduces a novel formulation that learns object Gaussians on an underlying 2D surface manifold rather than in 3D volume, yielding sharper, fine-grained object details for dynamic object reconstruction.

Unlike prior work that reconstructs only the human and treats objects as background, GASPACHO simultaneously recovers animatable templates for both the human and the interacting object as distinct sets of Gaussians, thereby allowing for controllable.
papers.title: GASPACHO: Gaussian Splatting for Controllable Humans and Objects

key_contributions: This work introduces SDD-4DGS, the first framework for static-dynamic decoupled 4D scene reconstruction based on Gaussian Splatting.

With carefully designed implementation strategies to realize this theoretical framework, the method effectively facilitates explicit learning of motion patterns for dynamic elements while maintaining geometric stability for static structures.

Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that SDD-4DGS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in reconstruction fidelity, with enhanced detail restoration for static structures and precise modeling of dynamic motions.
papers.title: SDD-4DGS: Static-Dynamic Aware Decoupling in Gaussian Splatting for 4D Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: To address this, the paper proposes Motion Blender Gaussian Splatting (MBGS), a novel framework that uses motion graphs as an explicit and sparse motion representation.
Supports novel-pose animation, robot-demonstration synthesis, and visual-planning-based robot action prediction.
Experiments show that MBGS achieves state-of-the-art performance on the highly challenging iPhone dataset while being competitive on HyperNeRF.
papers.title: Motion Blender Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Defines Gaussians jointly over spatial, temporal, and angular dimensions to model dynamics and view-dependent appearance in one representation.
Conditionally slices the 7D primitives into view- and time-specific 3D Gaussians that can be rendered with splatting.
Captures temporal motion and angular effects while retaining high real-time rendering throughput.
papers.title: 7DGS: Unified Spatial-Temporal-Angular Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Distills semantic context from a segmentation model into self-supervised 4D Gaussian features for driving scenes.
Tracks temporal deformation while compensating spatial features with a deformation-aware convolutional module.
Combines photometric reconstruction and contextual understanding for dynamic autonomous-driving view synthesis.
papers.title: CoDa-4DGS: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting with Context and Deformation Awareness for Autonomous Driving

key_contributions: To address these requirements, the paper introduces FeatureEndo-4DGS (FE-4DGS), the first real time pipeline leveraging feature-distilled 4D Gaussian Splatting for simultaneous reconstruction and semantic segmentation of deformable surgical environments.

Unlike prior feature-distilled methods restricted to static scenes, and existing 4D approaches that lack semantic integration, FE-4DGS seamlessly leverages pre-trained 2D semantic embeddings to produce a unified 4D representation-where semantics also deform with tissue motion.
This unified approach enables the generation of real-time RGB and semantic outputs through a single, parallelized rasterization process.
papers.title: Feature-EndoGaussian: Feature Distilled Gaussian Splatting in Surgical Deformable Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Presents Persistent Object Gaussian Splat (POGS), a system that embeds semantics, self-supervised visual features, and object grouping features into a compact representation that can be continuously updated to estimate the pose of scanned objects.
POGS updates object states without requiring expensive rescanning or prior CAD models of objects.

After an initial multi-view scene capture and training phase, POGS uses a single stereo camera to integrate depth estimates along with self-supervised vision encoder features for object pose estimation.
papers.title: Persistent Object Gaussian Splat (POGS) for Tracking Human and Robot Manipulation of Irregularly Shaped Objects

key_contributions: Evolves a Gaussian representation frame by frame through control-node deformation followed by detail refinement.
Adds and contribution-prunes a minimal number of Gaussians to handle topology changes and disocclusions.
Differentially encodes temporal updates for more than 50-fold compression while preserving fast explicit rendering.
papers.title: EvolvingGS: High-Fidelity Streamable Volumetric Video via Evolving 3D Gaussian Representation

key_contributions: To address these challenges, the paper proposes the NTR-Gaussian method, which treats temperature as a form of thermal radiation, incorporating elements like convective heat transfer and radiative heat dissipation.
Furthermore, the paper introduces a dynamic dataset specifically for nighttime thermal imagery.

Extensive experiments and evaluations demonstrate that NTR-Gaussian significantly outperforms comparison methods in thermal reconstruction, achieving a predicted temperature error within 1 degree Celsius.
papers.title: NTR-Gaussian: Nighttime Dynamic Thermal Reconstruction with 4D Gaussian Splatting Based on Thermodynamics

key_contributions: Proposes a novel framework leveraging generative 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models to extract and re-simulate 3D dynamic fluid objects from single-view videos using simulation methods.
The fluid geometry represented by 3DGS is initially generated and optimized from single-view images, then denoised, densified, and aligned across frames.
Estimates the fluid surface velocity using optical flow, propose a mainstream extraction algorithm to refine it.
papers.title: 3D Dynamic Fluid Assets from Single-View Videos with Generative Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces Efficient Dynamic Gaussian Splatting, which allocates time-varying attributes only to genuinely deformable regions of monocular dynamic scenes.
Represents motion with a sparse anchor grid and computes dense-Gaussian flow through a classical kernel formulation.
Uses unsupervised static-anchor filtering to reduce redundant Gaussians, improve rendering speed, and suppress jitter in static regions.
papers.title: Efficient Gaussian Splatting for Monocular Dynamic Scene Rendering via Sparse Time-Variant Attribute Modeling

key_contributions: This paper proposes a highly scalable method for dynamic novel view synthesis with continual learning.
Leverages the 3D Gaussians to represent the scene and a low-rank adaptation-based deformation model to capture the dynamic scene changes.
The method continuously reconstructs the dynamics with chunks of video frames, reduces the streaming bandwidth by while maintaining high rendering quality comparable to the off-line SOTA methods.
papers.title: Efficient 4D Gaussian Stream with Low Rank Adaptation

key_contributions: To address these limitations, the paper presents BEAM, a novel pipeline that bridges 4D Gaussian representations with physically-based rendering (PBR) to produce high-quality, relightable volumetric videos from multi-view RGB footage.

Generates roughness via a multi-view-conditioned diffusion model, and then derive AO and base color using a 2D-to-3D strategy, incorporating a tailored Gaussian-based ray tracer for efficient visibility computation.
BEAM recovers detailed geometry and PBR properties via a series of available Gaussian-based techniques.
papers.title: BEAM: Bridging Physically-based Rendering and Gaussian Modeling for Relightable Volumetric Video

key_contributions: Separates static and dynamic Gaussian content so text-guided edits can be applied to the canonical static representation.
Uses score-distillation guidance without repeatedly editing every video frame.
Adds temporal refinement to correct deformation-induced misalignment and propagate coherent edits through time.
papers.title: Instruct-4DGS: Efficient Dynamic Scene Editing via 4D Gaussian-based Static-Dynamic Separation

key_contributions: Presents Endo-2DTAM, a real-time endoscopic SLAM system with 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) to address these challenges.

The robust tracking module combines point-to-point and point-to-plane distance metrics, while the mapping module utilizes normal consistency and depth distortion to enhance surface reconstruction quality.

Extensive experiments on public endoscopic datasets demonstrate that Endo-2DTAM achieves an RMSE of mm for depth reconstruction of surgical scenes while maintaining computationally efficient tracking, high-quality visual appearance, and real-time rendering.
papers.title: Advancing Dense Endoscopic Reconstruction with Gaussian Splatting-driven Surface Normal-aware Tracking and Mapping

key_contributions: Introduces GaussianAvatar-Editor, an innovative framework for text-driven editing of animatable Gaussian head avatars that can be fully controlled in expression, pose, and viewpoint.
To address these issues, the paper proposes the Weighted Alpha Blending Equation (WABE).
Unlike static 3D Gaussian editing, editing animatable 4D Gaussian avatars presents challenges related to motion occlusion and spatial-temporal inconsistency.
papers.title: GaussianAvatar-Editor: Photorealistic Animatable Gaussian Head Avatar Editor

key_contributions: Decomposes motion into a global canonical scaffold for coarse movement and local Gaussian deformation for fine details.
Introduces temporal interval adjustment so motion parameters are allocated where scene dynamics require them.
Reduces model size while preserving reconstruction quality and real-time rendering.
papers.title: MoDec-GS: Global-to-Local Motion Decomposition and Temporal Interval Adjustment for Compact Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Represents continuous dynamic 3D Gaussian trajectories with motion-adaptive cubic Hermite splines and a small set of control points.
Progressively prunes trajectory control points according to each Gaussian's motion while preserving its deformation capacity.
Jointly optimizes camera parameters and Gaussian attributes, enabling COLMAP-free monocular reconstruction and fast rendering.
papers.title: SplineGS: Robust Motion-Adaptive Spline for Real-Time Dynamic 3D Gaussians from Monocular Video

key_contributions: Builds a multi-level Temporal Gaussian Hierarchy whose segments model scene regions with different rates of change.
Shares unchanged 4D Gaussian primitives across temporal segments and queries only relevant hierarchy subsets at each timestamp.
Keeps GPU memory nearly constant with video length while supporting minutes-long volumetric video and compact appearance storage.
papers.title: Representing Long Volumetric Video with Temporal Gaussian Hierarchy

key_contributions: Introduces a generalizable model that directly predicts 4D Gaussians from surround-view driving videos.
Uses a prune-and-dilate block to reduce overlapping adjacent-view Gaussians and redundant background points.
Decouples dynamic and static content to learn geometry and motion features across time.
papers.title: DrivingRecon: Large 4D Gaussian Reconstruction Model For Autonomous Driving

key_contributions: Trains a Gaussian-avatar prior on synthetic data, then fits and fine-tunes it to a single photo or video.
Produces animatable avatars with 360-degree rendering from limited monocular capture.
Uses the prior only during fitting, enabling real-time rendering after reconstruction.
papers.title: GASP: Gaussian Avatars with Synthetic Priors

key_contributions: Recasts continuous dynamic representation estimation within exposure time as exposure-time estimation.
Uses exposure, multi-frame, and multi-resolution consistency regularization to avoid trivial solutions.
Introduces blur-aware variable canonical Gaussians for objects with large motion.
papers.title: Deblur4DGS: 4D Gaussian Splatting from Blurry Monocular Video

key_contributions: Optimizes Gaussian primitives directly in 4D space for high-quality real-time rendering of temporally complex scenes.
Introduces a scale-aware residual field that incorporates primitive size and aligns with Gaussian self-splitting behavior.
Uses an adaptive optimization schedule based on temporal properties to accelerate reconstruction of dynamic regions.
papers.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting with Scale-aware Residual Field and Adaptive Optimization for Real-time Rendering of Temporally Complex Dynamic Scenes

key_contributions: Prunes Gaussians using temporal relevance and applies gradient-aware mixed-precision quantization to dynamic attributes.
Compresses Gaussian trajectories with Ramer–Douglas–Peucker keypoint selection and interpolation.
Reports up to 67-fold compression with minimal or no loss of visual quality.
papers.title: Temporally Compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scenes

key_contributions: To tackle this problem, in this paper, the paper proposes a novel approach to automatically discover the associated skeleton model for dynamic objects from videos without the need for object-specific templates.
Besides, an adaptive control strategy is applied to avoid the emergence of redundant superpoints.
Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the method in obtaining re-posable 3D objects.
papers.title: Template-free Articulated Gaussian Splatting for Real-time Reposable Dynamic View Synthesis

key_contributions: Encodes a dynamic sequence as Gaussian-attribute residuals between consecutive frames instead of retransmitting complete representations.
Quantizes non-position attributes with a latent decoder and sparsifies position residuals with learned gating.
Uses view-space gradient changes to identify dynamic content, reporting about 0.7 MB per frame, under five-second training, and 350 FPS rendering.
papers.title: QUEEN: QUantized Efficient ENcoding of Dynamic Gaussians for Streaming Free-viewpoint Videos

key_contributions: Organizes, benchmark, and analyze many Gaussian-splatting-based methods, providing apples-to-apples comparisons that prior works have lacked.
Uses multiple existing datasets and a new instructive synthetic dataset designed to isolate factors that affect reconstruction quality.
Categorizes Gaussian splatting methods into specific motion representation types and quantify how their differences impact performance.
papers.title: Monocular Dynamic Gaussian Splatting: Fast, Brittle, and Scene Complexity Rules

key_contributions: Introduces DGNS, a hybrid framework integrating Deformable Gaussian Splatting and Dynamic Neural Surfaces, effectively addressing dynamic novel-view synthesis and 3D geometry reconstruction simultaneously.

During training, depth maps generated by the deformable Gaussian splatting module guide the ray sampling for faster processing and provide depth supervision within the dynamic neural surface module to improve geometry reconstruction.
Extensive experiments conducted on public datasets demonstrate that DGNS achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D reconstruction, along with competitive results in novel-view synthesis.
papers.title: DGNS: Deformable Gaussian Splatting and Dynamic Neural Surface for Monocular Dynamic 3D Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces a motion-aware feed-forward model for bullet-time reconstruction and novel-view synthesis from casual monocular video.
Aggregates all context frames to reconstruct a 3D Gaussian scene at a selected target timestamp.
Uses a formulation intended to train across both static and dynamic scene datasets.
papers.title: Feed-Forward Bullet-Time Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes from Monocular Videos

key_contributions: Reconstructs casual monocular videos by separating static and dynamic Gaussians and estimating camera motion and depth.
Regularizes geometry, surfaces, and continuous motion to encourage physically plausible and temporally consistent reconstruction.
Introduces Kubric-MRig with broad camera and object motion and synchronized multi-view observations.
papers.title: RoDyGS: Robust Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Casual Videos

key_contributions: Unveils a fresh approach that blends state-space modeling with Wasserstein geometry, paving the way for a more fluid and coherent representation of dynamic scenes.
Introduces a State Consistency Filter that merges prior predictions with the current observations, enabling Gaussians to stay true to their way over time.
The approach guides Gaussians along their natural way in the Wasserstein space, achieving smoother, more realistic motion and stronger temporal coherence.
papers.title: Gaussians on their Way: Wasserstein-Constrained 4D Gaussian Splatting with State-Space Modeling

key_contributions: Introduces a novel 4D anchor-based framework that tackles the storage cost in different perspective.
Rather than reducing the number of Gaussians, the method retains a sufficient quantity to accurately model dynamic contents, while compressing them into compact, grid-aligned 4D anchor features.
Experimental results highlight that the method achieves state-of-the-art visual quality in dynamic regions, outperforming all baselines by a large margin with practical storage costs.
papers.title: 4D Scaffold Gaussian Splatting with Dynamic-Aware Anchor Growing for Efficient and High-Fidelity Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

key_contributions: Models avatar deformation with hierarchical motion context over skeleton and vertex motion.
Combines coarse skeleton motion with fine-grained vertex motion for non-rigid deformation.
Renders avatars orders of magnitude faster than temporal NeRF baselines.
papers.title: Sequential Gaussian Avatars with Hierarchical Motion Context

key_contributions: To address this, the paper proposes Explicit Motion Decomposition (EMD), which models the motions of dynamic objects by introducing learnable motion embeddings to the Gaussians, enhancing the decomposition in street scenes.
The proposed plug-and-play EMD module compensates for the lack of motion modeling in self-supervised street Gaussian splatting methods.
Introduces tailored training strategies to extend EMD to supervised approaches.
papers.title: EMD: Explicit Motion Modeling for High-Quality Street Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Introduces SplatFlow, a Self-Supervised Dynamic Gaussian Splatting within Neural Motion Flow Fields (NMFF) to learn 4D space-time representations without requiring tracked 3D bounding boxes, enabling accurate dynamic scene reconstruction and novel view RGB/depth/flow synthesis.

SplatFlow designs a unified framework to seamlessly integrate time-dependent 4D Gaussian representation within NMFF, where NMFF is a set of implicit functions to model temporal motions of both LiDAR points and Gaussians as continuous motion.
Leveraging NMFF, SplatFlow effectively decomposes static background and dynamic objects, representing them with 3D and 4D Gaussian primitives, respectively.
papers.title: SplatFlow: Self-Supervised Dynamic Gaussian Splatting in Neural Motion Flow Field for Autonomous Driving

key_contributions: Uses selective inheritance to carry reliable Gaussians between timestamps and preserve temporal continuity during online reconstruction.
Introduces a dynamics-aware shift that separates static and dynamic primitives and moves the dynamic subset efficiently.
Applies error-guided densification to emerging content and reports fast training with real-time rendering.
papers.title: Dynamics-Aware Gaussian Splatting Streaming Towards Fast On-the-Fly 4D Reconstruction

key_contributions: Introduces Dynamic Gaussian Splatting SLAM (DGS-SLAM), the first dynamic SLAM framework built on the foundation of Gaussian Splatting.

Within this framework, to further improve the accuracy of dynamic object removal, the paper introduces a robust mask generation method that enforces photometric consistency across keyframes, reducing noise from inaccurate segmentation and artifacts such as.

To address these challenges, the method integrates Gaussian Splatting SLAM with a robust filtering process to handle dynamic objects throughout the entire pipeline, including Gaussian insertion and keyframe selection.
papers.title: DGS-SLAM: Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environment

key_contributions: Quantifies uncertainty from each Gaussian's contribution to training-image rendering and constructs uncertainty maps for unseen views.
Selectively applies diffusion and depth-smoothness priors to uncertain regions, reducing over-regularization of well-observed content.
Densifies fast-moving dynamic regions using estimated depth and scene flow where structure-from-motion initialization is unreliable.
papers.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild with Uncertainty-Aware Regularization

key_contributions: To address this problem, the paper proposes DG-SLAM, the first robust dynamic visual SLAM system grounded in 3D Gaussians, which provides precise camera pose estimation alongside high-fidelity reconstructions.

Specifically, the paper proposes effective strategies, including motion mask generation, adaptive Gaussian point management, and a hybrid camera tracking algorithm to improve the accuracy and robustness of pose estimation.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that DG-SLAM delivers state-of-the-art performance in camera pose estimation, map reconstruction, and novel-view synthesis in dynamic scenes, outperforming existing methods meanwhile preserving real-time rendering ability.
papers.title: DG-SLAM: Robust Dynamic Gaussian Splatting SLAM with Hybrid Pose Optimization

key_contributions: Builds a compact initial representation with perturbation smoothing, then learns nonuniform motion through hierarchical local Gaussian coherence.
Merges newly added Gaussians into the representation while removing an equal number of low-opacity primitives to constrain stream size.
Reports about 85% lower storage, roughly 20% higher learning efficiency, and under two seconds per frame with parallel processing.
papers.title: HiCoM: Hierarchical Coherent Motion for Streamable Dynamic Scene with 3D Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Replaces low-rank planes with one spatial and three temporal 3D hash encodings for a decomposed 4D representation.
Uses directional attention to aggregate spatial and temporal features according to local scene context.
Adds smoothness regularization to stabilize deformation prediction from the explicit hash representation.
papers.title: Grid4D: 4D Decomposed Hash Encoding for High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Learns object dynamics from multi-view RGB robot-interaction videos while accounting for action trajectories and 3D scene states.
Trains a graph neural dynamics model on sparse control particles downsampled from tracked 3D Gaussians.
Interpolates Gaussian transformations from predicted control-particle motion to render action-conditioned future states.
papers.title: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Tracking for Graph-Based Neural Dynamics Modeling

key_contributions: Separates static and dynamic Gaussians and explicitly samples dynamic positions and rotations at sparse timestamps.
Interpolates sampled attributes to model spatially and temporally continuous object motion with lower cost.
Uses progressive training and point backtracking to improve convergence and remove erroneous Gaussians.
papers.title: Fully Explicit Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

key_contributions: Replaces high-dimensional per-Gaussian spherical-harmonic color attributes with direct color and a shared lightweight color predictor.
Introduces entropy-constrained Gaussian deformation and opacity-based entropy loss to limit Gaussian count.
Combines the representation with half-precision storage and zip compression.
papers.title: MEGA: Memory-Efficient 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scenes

key_contributions: Identifies canonical-coordinate noise as a source of corruption that propagates into dynamic Gaussian deformation fields.
Introduces a noise-suppression strategy that changes the canonical coordinate distribution to reduce deformation noise.
